independence: RHMZ event warnings and the climatologist interview support Banat; Wikipedia's gorge maximum is a partly separate climatology-textbook line. The public long-term abstract does not adjudicate the ranking.
missing_definition: Specify station, period, mean speed versus gust, frequency threshold and whether gorge-point or populated regional maxima are compared.
editor_conclusion: Say «the strongest measured regional gusts are characteristic of southern Banat, especially Vršac, while the gorge entrance has intense local jet acceleration».

comparison: The standard Croatian encyclopedia and HR Wikipedia give exactly the koş + hava derivation. Because HR copies the encyclopedia and the Turkish gloss is historically mediated, this is one lexicographic tradition rather than a six-language consensus.
independence: Hrvatska enciklopedija is the main authority; HR Wikipedia is derivative and the other five requested Wikipedias are silent.
missing_definition: Attribute the derivation and gloss hava as «air/weather»; a historical Ottoman-Turkish dictionary citation would strengthen the exact semantics of koş.
editor_conclusion: Write «the conventional etymology derives the name from Turkish koş + hava, roughly “fast air”» rather than presenting each gloss as undisputed modern Turkish.

comparison: Košava is predominantly a cold-season wind, but EN and SR explicitly describe it in summer and Serbian reports document May and warm-season events. October–April is not an exclusive season and «almost absent» needs actual monthly frequencies.
independence: Peer-reviewed climatology establishes cold-season prevalence; Serbian observations and the encyclopedic/Wikipedia corpus independently disprove a hard seasonal boundary.
missing_definition: Give monthly event-day or gust-frequency climatology for a fixed station network and period.
editor_conclusion: Replace with «most frequent from autumn to spring, but it also occurs in the growing season, including summer».

comparison: The conclusion depends on the false premise that Košava is absent during growth. General vineyard field evidence shows sustained wind can change shoot growth, canopy geometry, radiation and ripening conditions and can cause mechanical or reproductive damage.
independence: A peer-reviewed vineyard field study and university extension synthesis are independent of the Košava climatology; no Serbian vineyard trial quantifies local magnitude.
missing_definition: Measure growing-season Košava hours/gusts at vineyard height together with shoot damage, leaf conductance, evapotranspiration, flowering, berry temperature and ripening by site.
missing_descriptors: No wine aroma or flavour descriptor can be causally assigned to Košava from the selected evidence.
editor_conclusion: Delete «does not affect». Use «its viticultural effect is site- and timing-dependent and has not been quantified here».

comparison: Expert Serbian climatology supports a foehn-like leeward warm/dry pattern west of the eastern mountains, but peer-reviewed work defines Košava first as synoptic gap flow and warm/cold variants occur. Not every event or all of Banat/Podunavlje follows one thermodynamic path.
independence: The local expert explanation supplies the spatial foehn claim; general foehn physics and the peer-reviewed gap-flow analysis qualify rather than independently reproduce it.
missing_definition: Specify event type, upstream humidity, barrier cross-section, windward precipitation and observed lee temperature/humidity change.
editor_conclusion: Keep as a common leeward regime, not the universal definition of Košava; say «can warm and dry foehn-like on descent».

comparison: The windward Timok/Negotin contrast—cloud, fog, cold and weak rain/snow while the west is drier—is reported by a Serbian climatologist and repeatedly appears in RHMZ forecasts. It is recurrent but not guaranteed for every Košava event.
independence: Expert climatology gives the mechanism and RHMZ operational events independently demonstrate the pattern; requested Wikipedias largely omit it.
missing_definition: Use «Тимокской Краине» in Russian; define windward sector and separate orographic cloud from frontal precipitation.
editor_conclusion: Retain with «often/can» and correct «Тимочкой» to «Тимокской».

comparison: The Negotin municipality explicitly reports several days of fine snow with local winter Košava, while DE and RU mention snow or blizzards more broadly and RHMZ events show granular snow/freezing precipitation. The exact multi-day fine-snow descriptor is local and not universal.
independence: Municipal description, encyclopedia/Wikipedia summaries and RHMZ event reports provide three differently sourced lines, but only the municipality gives both duration and fine texture.
missing_definition: Specify Negotin/Timok locality, event dates, snow type and observed duration; distinguish snow carried by wind from locally precipitating snow.
editor_conclusion: Qualify as «in the Negotin/Timok windward sector, winter episodes can bring several days of fine snow».

comparison: Viticulture guidance and general water-body physics support temperature moderation near large unfrozen water, but neither Wikipedia nor selected field research quantifies winter frost reduction beside Serbian Danube vineyards. Ice, wind and cold-air drainage can reverse or overwhelm the effect.
independence: Industry best practice supports the first-order mechanism; peer-reviewed river studies show real temperature effects but in summer urban settings, not the claimed winter vineyard case.
missing_definition: Measure water and air temperature, humidity, wind, stability and vine-height minima along bank-normal transects through frost events, including ice-covered days.
editor_conclusion: Retain «can moderate near-bank temperatures» and remove any implication of a guaranteed frost-protection magnitude.

comparison: A universal «hundreds, not kilometres» limit is false as a general river-microclimate rule: measured/modelled cases range from 50 m to roughly 1.7 km. The winter Serbian Danube footprint remains unknown, so neither end of that range can be transferred directly.
independence: Two peer-reviewed case studies with very different widths and methods independently demonstrate strong context dependence; English Wikipedia provides no adjudicating distance.
missing_definition: Specify effect variable, season, hour, river width, background wind and threshold; run winter vineyard transects rather than assigning one distance class.
editor_conclusion: Replace the fixed limit with «the footprint varies from tens of metres to kilometres; it has not been measured here».

comparison: The Danube can form disruptive ice in severe winters, directly documented across the Serbian reach in 2017. Long records also show that full/extended freezing is now rare and spatially uneven, so the sentence should not imply a normal modern winter condition.
independence: Official Serbian operations records and a peer-reviewed lower-Danube historical series independently converge on possibility plus declining frequency.
missing_definition: Distinguish shore ice, drifting ice, ice jam, partial cover and complete freeze; give reach and year.
editor_conclusion: Keep with «can develop extensive ice in severe winters, although this has become rare».

comparison: Measured river environments affect temperature, humidity and heat stress, while the Douro vineyard study documents cold pools and fog interactions and explicitly says the water body's exact winter role is unknown. Winter frost moderation cannot exhaust the river's climatic influence.
independence: Peer-reviewed urban-river measurements and a seven-year vineyard-valley record use different settings and methods but both demonstrate multiple relevant variables.
missing_definition: List season-specific mechanisms—heat storage/exchange, breeze, humidity/fog and valley inversions—and quantify only those measured locally.
editor_conclusion: Delete «its role is exhausted by this»; describe several conditional river and valley effects.

comparison: The reflected-light narrative is explicit for Mosel in EN Wikipedia and NASA, so the book correctly reports that such a claim exists. The selected corpus does not establish its frequency across literature or a comparable Douro consensus.
independence: NASA's caption cites a wine-science book and contemporary Wikipedia, so NASA and EN Wikipedia are not fully independent confirmations; other requested Wikipedias are silent.
missing_definition: Separate «a recurring regional narrative» from measured extra irradiance and document Mosel and Douro independently.
editor_conclusion: Write «English-language descriptions of the Mosel often claim…» unless a separate Douro source is added.

comparison: EN Wikipedia's 0.06 open-ocean value, RU Wikipedia's 5% line and peer-reviewed observations support the few-percent/high-Sun order and a lower common value than grass/bare soil. All technical sources also say angle, spectrum, cloud and waves matter.
independence: Wikipedia tables overlap common reference traditions, while two independent peer-reviewed observing programmes establish variability.
missing_definition: State broadband or visible band, direct versus diffuse irradiance, solar zenith interval, wind/wave condition and whether albedo or directional reflectance is meant.
editor_conclusion: Keep «typically about 3–8% under high Sun» and add the measurement conditions; avoid presenting it as a universal river value.

comparison: Water reflectivity does rise at grazing incidence and can make strong low-Sun glint, as EN/DE Wikipedia, NOAA and peer-reviewed observations agree. «Only at sunset» is an imprecise temporal substitute for an angular and atmospheric condition.
independence: NOAA's geometric explanation and two observational albedo studies independently converge; EN/DE Wikipedia summarise the same physics.
missing_definition: Use solar zenith/elevation and direct/diffuse conditions rather than clock time; include wave-slope distribution.
editor_conclusion: Replace with «reflectivity rises sharply at grazing incidence, especially under clear low Sun».

comparison: Specular reflection fixes an angle relative to each local water facet, not a universal compass direction. Depending on azimuth and valley geometry, a reflected ray can reach a facing slope; EN Wikipedia and NASA's Mosel narrative directly conflict with «not upward on the slope» as an absolute.
independence: NOAA supplies first-principles geometry; NASA/EN Wikipedia supply a real wine-valley counter-narrative, though not a measured effect size.
missing_definition: Model solar azimuth/elevation, river centreline, water level and roughness, slope aspect/angle and vine position for each site.
editor_conclusion: Replace the directional prohibition with «only slopes lying in the glint geometry can receive it».

comparison: No selected experiment, Wikipedia article or public wine database establishes a universal kilometre distance at which reflected light becomes negligible to vines. The Mosel examples are commonly adjacent to the river, so they do not test the book's kilometre premise.
independence: The physical sources establish directional reflection and variable albedo but none measures receiver irradiance at the claimed vineyard distance.
missing_definition: Calculate direct, diffuse and reflected shortwave irradiance at canopy height or deploy paired pyranometers/radiometers across slope distances and phenological seasons.
editor_conclusion: Remove «nothing appreciable» unless a site-specific radiative budget and detection threshold are supplied.

comparison: Forests and windbreaks can buffer exposure and canopy temperatures, especially in advective cold, but vineyard guidance warns they can worsen radiation frost by blocking drainage. The book's first half is therefore conditional, not a general slope rule.
independence: Viticulture best practice, university extension and peer-reviewed forest microclimate measurements converge on regime and site dependence.
missing_definition: Distinguish forest interior/edge from a windbreak, advective from radiation frost, barrier porosity and the vine's position relative to cold-air flow.
editor_conclusion: Say «forest may reduce advective exposure or buffer its interior, but it does not universally suppress slope frost».

comparison: Cold air drains downslope and pools in hollows during radiation frost, and vegetation/windbreak barriers can dam or redirect it, raising risk in the backed-up zone. The coldest pocket may lie uphill of the barrier or in a neighbouring hollow, not automatically «below» the forest.
independence: BC vineyard practice directly addresses barriers; UGA explains slope drainage; forest and Douro sensor networks independently demonstrate complex cold pools and inversions.
missing_definition: Map the barrier's height/porosity, slope cross-section, drainage direction and vine-height temperature field during calm clear nights.
editor_conclusion: Retain the two-sided warning and replace fixed «lowlands below it» with «where the altered drainage causes cold air to pond».

comparison: The 2019 register clearly concentrates parcel counts at 100–300 m and puts only 26.80% above 300 m, so a broad 100–400 m shorthand is plausible. The book says vineyards without defining parcel count versus area and the accessible prose does not isolate the 300–400 and above-400 shares needed to compute the exact interval.
independence: CEVVIN is the sole authoritative dataset located; Wikipedias and wine guides do not reproduce the national distribution, so this is source-supported but not independently replicated.
missing_definition: State the 2019 register date, denominator (parcel count or hectares), bin boundaries and the exact 100–400 m sum.
editor_conclusion: Write «most registered parcels are at low-to-mid elevations, especially 100–300 m» or publish the exact 100–400 calculation and metric.

comparison: CEVVIN gives 43.80% of registered Prokupac vineyard area in the above-300-to-400 m bin; rounding to 44% is correct.
independence: The figure is a national specialist-register result but is not independently replicated by the six Wikipedias or wine databases.
missing_definition: Retain the source date, registered commercial area denominator and the open/closed bin convention.
editor_conclusion: Keep 44%, attribute it to CEVVIN/register data and date the snapshot.

comparison: The accessible CEVVIN profile publishes the leading 300–400 m bin but not a 22% total above 400 m. No Wikipedia, public wine database or raw register table located in the selected corpus reproduces the 22% figure.
independence: All useful evidence traces to CEVVIN, and the needed higher-bin values are absent from the accessible prose.
missing_definition: Provide the original altitude table or graph values, register snapshot, denominator and the bins included in «above 400 m».
editor_conclusion: Remove the 22% figure until the underlying table is cited or attach the reproducible calculation.

comparison: CEVVIN gives 60.80% of registered Vranac vineyard area in the above-300-to-400 m bin; rounding to 61% is correct.
independence: The number is authoritative register-derived evidence but not independently reproduced by the requested Wikipedias or public wine guides.
missing_definition: State the register snapshot, hectares denominator and bin endpoints.
editor_conclusion: Keep 61%, attribute it to CEVVIN/register data and date it.

comparison: The national CEVVIN profile directly says Smederevka's largest altitude bin is 200–300 m at 37.11%. A claimed 50% at 100–200 m would necessarily make that lower bin larger, so the two statements cannot both describe the same dataset and denominator.
independence: The contradiction is within the authoritative specialist dataset; Wikipedias and other public databases are silent and do not arbitrate it.
missing_definition: Identify any older register snapshot or alternative population behind 50%; otherwise use the current CEVVIN percentage and bin.
editor_conclusion: Replace the sentence with «CEVVIN places the largest Smederevka share at 200–300 m (37.11%)» unless the book can document a different dataset.

comparison: Prokupac and Vranac provide two descriptive examples of later-ripening cultivars concentrated at 300–400 m, but very-late Smederevka is a counterexample at 200–300 m. The data show where registered plantings are, not that late cultivars biologically prefer higher ground.
independence: The ripening and distribution evidence comes from three CEVVIN profiles; general altitude research supports delayed phenology but cannot remove Serbia-specific historical and geographic confounding.
missing_definition: Test all cultivars with registered area by altitude while controlling for region, aspect, site climate, planting era and cultivar phenology.
editor_conclusion: Replace the general preference rule with named, dated distributions and label them observations rather than varietal preference.

comparison: All detailed meteorological sources support a usual temperature decrease with elevation, and vineyard studies often find later phenology or ripening higher up. They also show a variable lapse rate, aspect/radiation effects and exceptions, so harvest does not move later by a fixed amount solely because elevation rises.
independence: EN/HU Wikipedia supply general atmospheric physics and peer-reviewed Alpine vineyard observations independently demonstrate both common delay and site-specific exceptions.
missing_definition: Give local growing-season lapse rate and paired phenology/harvest observations for the same cultivar, aspect, management and years.
editor_conclusion: Keep «higher sites are generally cooler and often later» and add that aspect, circulation, inversion, cultivar and year can reverse or outweigh the pattern.

comparison: EN, DE, HU, RU and HR Wikipedia definitions agree that inversion reverses the normal vertical temperature gradient; EN/RU/DE and the Douro vineyard network support nocturnal downslope drainage, cold pooling and colder basin bottoms.
independence: The Wikipedias partly share a common meteorological tradition, while the seven-year vineyard sensor study independently measures the phenomenon.
missing_definition: Specify radiative/nocturnal inversion, clear calm conditions, sensor height and slope-versus-bottom elevation difference when quantifying a site.
editor_conclusion: Retain the explanation; replace any implication that every night or every basin produces an inversion with conditional wording.

comparison: Toplica's central depression is explicitly bracketed by Jastrebac and southern mountains, and Župa producer/regional descriptions consistently frame vineyards with Kopaonik, Željin, Goč and Jastrebac. Neither landscape is a perfectly sealed bowl, so «surrounded» is topographic shorthand.
independence: English and Serbian Wikipedia/encyclopedic geography support Toplica; the Župa line comes from local geographic and producer descriptions and is less independent.
missing_definition: Define the exact wine-region boundaries and map ridge elevations, passes and drainage outlets instead of treating an entire named region as one closed basin.
editor_conclusion: Keep the mountain-framed geography but say «lying among/between mountain massifs» rather than implying complete enclosure.

comparison: Trade and producer sources describe mountain shelter from harsh weather, making reduced advective exposure plausible. General basin meteorology also shows that enclosure can intensify cold pools, and no selected paired station record establishes fewer extremes or a longer frost-free season in both regions.
independence: Two local narratives cover Toplica and Župa separately, but neither is a controlled climatic analysis; the Douro study independently supplies the countervailing basin mechanism.
missing_definition: Compare ridge, slope and basin-bottom stations for minimum/maximum temperature, wind, first/last frost and frost-free or growing-degree-day season over a climatic normal.
editor_conclusion: Separate conditional wind shelter from the unproven claim of systematically moderated extremes and a longer season.

comparison: No source defines «sharply delineated» seasons or «rapid» transitions for Župa and Toplica, and no temperature or phenology time series is offered for comparison with another region.
independence: The six Wikipedias, CEVVIN, wein.plus, SerbianWine.rs and the selected climatology studies are silent on this exact qualitative claim.
missing_definition: Choose a metric such as duration between seasonal temperature thresholds, onset dates, variance and a comparator region, then analyse multi-decadal station records.
editor_conclusion: Remove the phrase or present it explicitly as literary impression, not audited climatology.

comparison: Cold-air pooling and nocturnal inversion are established consequences of enclosed low relief under suitable stable conditions. The general mechanism is sound, but the book supplies no local frequency, depth or frost-risk measurements for Župa and Toplica.
independence: Multiple Wikipedia editions converge on the mechanism and the Douro vineyard sensor network independently measures frequent valley cold pools; local occurrence remains an inference from topography.
missing_definition: Install vine-height and standard-height logger transects from basin floor to slope and report event frequency, temperature deficit, duration, wind and season.
editor_conclusion: Keep as a conditional terrain risk and add that its magnitude in each Serbian basin has not been measured in the cited corpus.

comparison: SerbianWine.rs and common wine communication treat local cultivars as voices of regional identity, but no source defines or measures «regional character» or isolates variety from terroir, cellar practice and producer choice.
independence: The available support is rhetorical and tourism-facing rather than an independent sensory, chemical or market study.
missing_definition: Define regional character, pre-register a blinded sensory/chemical comparison and control cultivar, site, vintage and winemaking.
missing_descriptors: Any descriptor attributed to a region must be separated from cultivar and production-method effects.
editor_conclusion: Retain only as an explicit editorial reason for ordering the appendix, not as an audited causal fact.

comparison: Both the 2019 register analysis and wein.plus's 2023 hectare table show clearly international or internationally widespread cultivars dominating the largest Serbian holdings. The exact margin changes with whether Graševina/Welschriesling and Frankovka are classified as regional or international.
independence: CEVVIN's ministry-register snapshot and wein.plus's later area table independently support the direction, though their dates and category schemes differ.
missing_definition: Publish totals by a declared taxonomy—autochthonous, regional/traditional, domestic-bred and international—and give the year and registered-versus-total scope.
editor_conclusion: Keep «international and internationally widespread varieties occupy more area», adding a date and classification caveat.

comparison: The «originated here» half matches strict autochthonous usage. The alternative «rooted here so long that origin is lost» is too broad: a long-established introduced cultivar can be traditional, local, regional or domesticated without being native, and unknown ancestry is not proof of origin.
independence: EN/DE terminology and a peer-reviewed grapevine study converge on indigenous origin; OIV separately supplies an age-based category, while Serbian official practice distinguishes autochthonous and regional groups.
missing_definition: For every cultivar state the evidence class: genetic/geographic origin, earliest documentation, current centre of diversity, introduced-but-traditional status, or unresolved origin.
editor_conclusion: Define autochthonous as native/originating locally; use «regional/traditional» for old introduced or uncertain-origin cultivars and preserve the cautionary note.

comparison: Rskavac is listed as a Prokupac synonym by EN and DE Wikipedia, CEVVIN, public wein.plus and the VIVC identity tradition.
independence: VIVC and CEVVIN are the primary identity anchors; Wikipedia and wein.plus partly reproduce the same ampelographic tradition rather than counting as wholly independent confirmations.
missing_definition: Distinguish the registered synonym from occasional commercial use of Rskavac for a selected old-vine expression or biotype.
editor_conclusion: Keep Rskavac as a synonym, optionally labelling it explicitly as such.

comparison: Kameničarka/Kamenicarka is consistently listed as a Prokupac synonym in EN and DE Wikipedia, CEVVIN, public wein.plus and the VIVC-linked identity record.
independence: The strongest independent Serbian and international identity authorities agree; secondary sites repeat that record.
editor_conclusion: Keep Kameničarka as a documented synonym.

comparison: SerbianWine.rs and a current Šumadija producer support medium body, while Budimir documents medium-plus and other published examples reach full body. Medium is representative but not a fixed ceiling.
independence: A national overview and producers from different regions show both the centre and range of contemporary styles; the peer-reviewed young/aged comparison also demonstrates matrix and age effects.
missing_definition: Body should be treated as a sensory style result influenced by alcohol, extract, tannin and production, not a cultivar constant.
missing_descriptors: Documented Prokupac styles also include lighter, medium-plus and full-bodied examples.
editor_conclusion: Keep «medium body» as a common style and add that versions range from light to full.

comparison: Freshness or vivid acidity is repeated by EN Wikipedia, SerbianWine.rs, CEVVIN and bottle-specific sources. The young/aged study finds greater perceived acidity in its young wine, showing that expression changes with age and matrix.
independence: Popular references, a national portal, producer analysis and peer-reviewed sensory chemistry converge on appreciable acidity, although not on one numerical range.
missing_definition: For technical use report total acidity, pH, vintage and sampling stage alongside the sensory term «lively».
editor_conclusion: Keep lively acidity as a recurring profile, not an invariant laboratory value.

comparison: Published examples span silky or soft tannins through pronounced structure, matching the stated range. Tannin level and quality depend heavily on extraction, fruit maturity and ageing.
independence: SerbianWine.rs, CEVVIN, multiple producers and peer-reviewed sensory work support variation rather than a single fixed level.
missing_definition: Separate tannin concentration from sensory quality—soft, ripe, coarse and astringent are not interchangeable measurements.
editor_conclusion: Keep the moderate-to-pronounced range and explicitly attribute variation to style and vinification.

comparison: The controlled young-versus-aged comparison supports greater acidity and astringency in the studied young Prokupac. It does not establish the subjective «coarse» quality for all young wines, and modern examples can have polished tannins.
independence: Peer-reviewed evidence is strong for selected wines; the broader tasting corpus demonstrates countervailing stylistic variation.
missing_definition: Define «coarse» through a trained sensory scale and report phenolic maturity, maceration, oak and bottle age.
editor_conclusion: Change the implied rule to «young, extraction-led examples can show conspicuous or coarse astringency».

comparison: CEVVIN explicitly links longer pomace contact to greater tannin extraction and potentially astringent Prokupac, while the young/aged study confirms substantial astringency in a selected young example. The outcome is technological, not automatic.
independence: A national technical profile and peer-reviewed sensory chemistry agree on the capacity for marked astringency through different evidence types.
missing_definition: Report maceration duration, temperature, cap management, seed maturity and ageing before attributing astringency to the variety alone.
editor_conclusion: Keep that Prokupac can be openly astringent, adding that extraction and maturity determine whether it is.

comparison: DE Wikipedia calls Prokupac late ripening, and CEVVIN places it between the third and fourth ripening epochs.
independence: The local technical source and an independent-language encyclopaedia converge on the same phenology.
missing_definition: If a calendar date is added later, specify region and vintage because ripening epochs are relative classifications.
editor_conclusion: Keep «late».

comparison: Thick berry skin is stated by DE Wikipedia and the Serbian CEVVIN ampelographic profile.
independence: German secondary and Serbian specialist sources converge; both are consistent with the cultivar identity literature.
editor_conclusion: Keep the thick-skin characteristic.

comparison: Cherry is the strongest recurring fruit family across SerbianWine.rs, professional comparative tasting, producers and the broad dark-fruit wording of EN Wikipedia.
independence: General profiles and multiple wines from different producers repeat sour, red, black or unspecified cherry without relying on one product page.
missing_definition: Translations should preserve whether the source says sour, red, black or generic cherry rather than flattening every form into one exact fruit.
editor_conclusion: Keep cherry as a core possible Prokupac descriptor.

comparison: Ripe/sweet cherry is explicit in a particular Aleksandrović Prokupac profile, but the independent corpus usually gives generic, sour or black cherry. Russian «черешня» is therefore narrower than much of the evidence.
independence: The direct sweet-cherry evidence is mainly producer-specific, while the broader independent evidence supports the adjacent cherry family.
missing_definition: Do not translate unqualified English cherry automatically as «черешня»; require sweet cherry or an equivalent original term.
editor_conclusion: Retain as an occasional ripe-fruit nuance, at lower confidence than вишня.

comparison: Raspberry recurs in the JancisRobinson.com comparative corpus and in bottle profiles including Budimir, supporting it as a possible red-fruit note.
independence: Professional multi-wine tasting and producer-specific evidence agree, although no descriptor is mandatory in every bottle.
editor_conclusion: Keep raspberry as a documented possible descriptor.

comparison: Plum is repeated in SerbianWine.rs, professional tastings and several producer profiles, ranging from fresh plum to damson and plum jam.
independence: National overview, independent tasting and producers from different sites all support the descriptor family.
missing_definition: Fresh plum, damson and jam indicate different ripeness/development and should not be treated as identical notes in a specific wine.
editor_conclusion: Keep plum as a core possible Prokupac descriptor.

comparison: Violet appears in the professional comparative corpus and specific Doajen and other wine profiles, but not in the short broad Wikipedia or SerbianWine.rs summaries.
independence: One high-quality multi-wine tasting and several bottle-specific descriptions support occurrence, not universality.
editor_conclusion: Keep violet as an occasional floral descriptor.

comparison: Pepper is repeatedly documented in professional tasting and producer profiles; where specified, white pepper is common. DE Wikipedia independently supports the broader spicy character.
independence: Professional, producer and encyclopaedic evidence converge across different levels of specificity.
missing_definition: If greater precision is wanted, distinguish white pepper from generic pepper and other spices.
editor_conclusion: Keep pepper as a well-supported possible descriptor.

comparison: The herbal family is well supported, but sources alternate among wild herbs, dried herbs, mint and generic herbal spice. Exact «dried herbs» has narrower support than the family as a whole.
independence: SerbianWine.rs, professional tasting and bottle-specific profiles agree on herbal character but not on one exact form.
missing_definition: Separate dried herbs from fresh mint and from green/herbaceous character associated with under-ripeness.
missing_descriptors: Mint appears in an oak-aged Župa example and can be listed separately when attributed to that wine.
editor_conclusion: Prefer «wild or dried herbs» for the broad profile; keep exact dried herbs only as a possible instance.

comparison: Earth or dry-earth character occurs in professional and producer descriptions, including Doajen. It is a sensory descriptor, not evidence that mineral soil components pass directly into wine flavour.
independence: Independent tasting and multiple bottle-specific sources support occurrence; Wikipedias do not list it.
missing_definition: Define earthiness as an aroma/flavour metaphor and avoid a causal terroir claim without chemical evidence.
editor_conclusion: Keep earthiness as an occasional sensory descriptor without literal soil causality.

comparison: Leather occurs in mature, oak-aged Budimir and in professional descriptions of developed Prokupac. The sources do not isolate bottle age from oak and vinification as the cause.
independence: Professional tasting and an official mature-wine profile agree on occurrence in particular wines.
missing_definition: Distinguish barrel age, bottle age and oxidative or microbial development when explaining tertiary notes.
editor_conclusion: Use «mature/aged examples can show leather», not a guaranteed age sequence.

comparison: Tobacco is documented in the professional corpus and in oak/amphora-aged Doajen, but can reflect wood-spice and maturation together rather than age alone.
independence: An independent multi-wine report and a technology-disclosing producer agree on occurrence.
missing_definition: Attribute tobacco as a possible tertiary or oak-associated note unless a controlled age comparison isolates the cause.
editor_conclusion: Keep as a possible developed-wine note with the oak/age caveat.

comparison: Forest floor is documented in professional tastings of some developed Prokupac wines, but no controlled series shows that ageing alone creates it in the cultivar.
independence: More than one professional bottle-level observation supports occurrence, while broad references remain silent.
missing_definition: Forest floor can combine damp leaf, earth and mushroom impressions; define the term if used for non-specialists.
missing_descriptors: Additional documented but non-universal Prokupac notes absent from the card include blackberry/other dark berries, currant, strawberry, mint, cedar, vanilla, clove, cinnamon, orange peel and mushroom; many are bottle-, ripeness- or oak-specific.
editor_conclusion: Retain only as a possible note in developed examples and add the definition/cause caveat.

comparison: EN Wikipedia, CEVVIN and SerbianWine.rs all identify Toplica as a principal Prokupac area.
independence: Encyclopaedic, national technical and wine-portal sources converge on the geography.
missing_definition: Clarify whether a name refers to the official wine region, a broader geographical area or a historical identity.
editor_conclusion: Keep Toplica in the regional list.

comparison: Župa is strongly supported: CEVVIN's register profile makes Župsko vinogorje the largest named Prokupac area, while SerbianWine.rs lists Župa. Administratively it sits within the wider Three Moravas wine region.
independence: Registered-area data and an independent national wine overview agree, though they use nested geographic levels.
missing_definition: State the hierarchy Župsko vinogorje / Three Moravas region when formal zoning matters.
editor_conclusion: Keep Župa, optionally clarifying its place within Three Moravas.

comparison: EN Wikipedia and SerbianWine.rs both list Šumadija for Prokupac. The three names in the book are valid but not exhaustive: Leskovac, the wider Three Moravas/Nišava-Toplica groupings and smaller plantings elsewhere are also documented.
independence: Encyclopaedic and Serbian wine-portal evidence converge, while CEVVIN supplies complementary registered geography.
missing_definition: Label the regional line as «main examples» rather than a complete distribution unless every official region is enumerated.
editor_conclusion: Keep Šumadija and mark the card's region list as selective rather than exhaustive.

comparison: SerbianWine.rs identifies Tamjanika as a signature variety of Župa and the wider Three Moravas route. The region is an important centre, not the cultivar's exclusive Serbian location.
independence: The national cultivar guide and a separate regional route page converge on the Župa association, but both belong to one portal and do not constitute planted-area statistics.
missing_definition: Distinguish Župa/Župsko vinogorje from the wider Three Moravas region and label the regional tag as a principal example.
editor_conclusion: Keep Župa, adding that Tamjanika is also grown elsewhere in Serbia.

comparison: EN Wikipedia, public wein.plus and SerbianWine.rs converge on white Tamjanika as a local Serbian expression/name within Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains. Shared Tamjanika naming for dark forms and inconsistent Tamjanika Bela records make an unqualified one-to-one identity too simple.
independence: The encyclopaedia, specialist lexicon and national guide agree on the core family, while their nomenclatural differences reveal the scope caveat.
missing_definition: State colour and accession: «white Tamjanika, generally identified with Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains»; reserve clone-level claims for genotyped material.
editor_conclusion: Keep «Мускат мелкоягодный» as a practical identity, adding the white-form/name-ambiguity qualification.

comparison: Jasmine is explicit in SerbianWine.rs and sits within the dominant floral family reported by the national wine association.
independence: A national guide gives the exact flower and an industry association independently supports strong floral character.
missing_descriptors: Other recurring floral specifics include elderflower and orange blossom.
editor_conclusion: Keep jasmine.

comparison: EN Wikipedia, SerbianWine.rs and multiple wine descriptions repeat the elder family, but wording varies among elderflower, elder plant and elderberry. Generic «бузина» is safe if not silently converted into one exact form.
independence: Encyclopaedic, national-guide and bottle-level sources converge on the family despite translation differences.
missing_definition: Preserve elderflower versus elderberry and avoid inventing elderflower syrup unless the source says syrup.
editor_conclusion: Keep generic бузина or specify flowers of elder when that is the cited original.

comparison: Citrus is repeatedly supported by SerbianWine.rs and the national association, with lemon peel, mandarin, orange and occasional grapefruit forms in the wider corpus.
independence: Two broad Serbian sources and individual wine profiles agree on the descriptor family.
missing_definition: Specific citrus types belong to particular wines and should not all be promised in one generic profile.
missing_descriptors: Repeated specifics include lemon peel, mandarin and orange blossom; grapefruit is less universal.
editor_conclusion: Keep citrus as a core descriptor family.

comparison: EN Wikipedia describes exceptionally strong grape aroma, while SerbianWine.rs and the national association consistently call white Tamjanika intensely aromatic. No source defines or measures a national top-ranking against every Serbian white cultivar.
independence: Encyclopaedic, national-guide and industry sources agree on intensity, though the ranking phrase is editorial.
missing_definition: A literal «one of the most» ranking would require a defined sensory or volatile-aroma comparison set and threshold.
missing_descriptors: Other common notes absent from the short card include orange blossom, grape, peach, basil, cinnamon and incense-like spice.
editor_conclusion: Keep «one of Serbia's intensely aromatic whites» as a qualitative description, not a measured ranking.

comparison: SerbianWine.rs directly describes a sweet aromatic impression in dry Tamjanika, and peer-reviewed sensory work supports aroma-enhanced sweetness in dry wine generally. The experiment did not isolate muscat terpenes, and sugar is not the only non-aromatic factor.
independence: A cultivar-specific industry observation aligns with independent cross-modal sensory science.
missing_definition: Separate analytical residual sugar, legal dry category and perceived sweetness; report alcohol and acidity where technical precision matters.
editor_conclusion: Keep the mechanism as «intense muscat-fruit aromas can enhance perceived sweetness», not as an exclusive cause.

comparison: Independent dry still Tamjanika pages recommend 8–12 °C and 8–10 °C, directly supporting the stated range for the common fresh style. The recommendation does not automatically cover sweet, sparkling, orange or oak-aged versions.
independence: Two different producers/import channels give consistent service guidance.
missing_definition: Attach the range to fresh still dry Tamjanika and give separate recommendations only when a different style is discussed.
editor_conclusion: Keep 8–12 °C with a style qualifier.

comparison: Peer-reviewed history, Slow Food, SerbianWine.rs and current producers document a strong Negotin/Negotinska Krajina association. Historical Srem records and modern wines elsewhere show that Negotin is a centre, not the exclusive location.
independence: Academic history, an international heritage project, a national directory and producer records converge through different channels.
missing_definition: Use Negotin/Negotinska Krajina as a principal Serbian association, not as a claim of exclusive origin or distribution.
editor_conclusion: Keep Negotin with a non-exclusivity qualification.

comparison: DE Wikipedia, VIVC and public wein.plus identify Tamjanika Crna/Krajinska Tamjanika Crna with Rosenmuskateller/Moscato Rosa, a rare red-skinned aromatic Muscat-group cultivar. It should not be reduced to a generic colour mutation of white Tamjanika.
independence: The international database and specialist lexicon are identity anchors; Wikipedia supplies an independently edited, more readable profile.
missing_definition: Add Rosenmuskateller/Moscato Rosa and distinguish this cultivar from white Tamjanika.
missing_descriptors: Across styles the strongest recurring descriptors are rose/rose oil, floral spice and red fruit; sweetness varies from dry to dessert wine.
editor_conclusion: Keep «aromatic red Muscat», adding the precise identity and colour-form warning.

comparison: EN and DE Wikipedia call the cultivar rare, while the academic and Slow Food records document fragmented old material and active preservation in Serbia.
independence: Encyclopaedic, genetic-historical and biodiversity sources agree on rarity and conservation significance.
missing_definition: If quantified rarity is needed, report registered hectares, accessions or producer count for a stated year.
editor_conclusion: Keep «rare».

comparison: Late-harvest and overripe grapes are directly documented for Matalj and repeated for some Negotin wines, but dry Crna Tamjanika styles also exist and no source gives the market share or frequency needed for «often». Some examples are harvested in late September without documented raisining.
independence: Producer/retail records confirm the practice in multiple labels, while current dry wines provide counterexamples to a universal or clearly dominant method.
missing_definition: Define «later than term» relative to physiological maturity and publish harvest dates, berry weight loss and proportion of wines using late harvest.
editor_conclusion: Replace «often harvested late» with «some Negotin versions use late-harvest or overripe grapes».

comparison: Matalj's archived description supports rapid on-vine dehydration and shrivelling of overripe Crna Tamjanika, but no checked source defines a stage called polusuvarak or equates it quantitatively to a half-raisin.
independence: The positive evidence is effectively one wine narrative repeated by retailers; encyclopaedias and scientific papers do not use the local term.
missing_definition: Give berry mass loss, soluble solids, visual scale and a Serbian source defining polusuvarak before treating it as a technical stage.
editor_conclusion: Retain only as attributed local speech—«berries may partly shrivel on the vine»—not a standardized stage.

comparison: The Matalj example and peer-reviewed physiology agree that water loss concentrates must. The mechanism is concentration by dehydration, not necessarily creation of more sugar per berry, and composition changes are not uniform.
independence: A cultivar-specific wine record aligns with independent viticulture and aroma experiments in other cultivars.
missing_definition: Specify whether concentration refers to °Brix, residual sugar, extract, acids, phenolics or aroma compounds; these do not change identically.
editor_conclusion: Keep concentration as a water-loss effect, naming the measured component and avoiding a blanket statement.

comparison: Crna Tamjanika is strongly aromatic even in non-raisined styles, and dehydration can concentrate or transform volatile compounds. The evidence does not show that half-raisining alone creates its aromatic density or explains why growers preserve it.
independence: DE Wikipedia, Slow Food and multiple wines establish inherent muscat-floral intensity; independent dehydration science complicates the book's single-cause chain.
missing_definition: Separate inherent varietal aroma from changes due to overripeness, water loss, fermentation and sweetness, and define «density» through sensory intensity or chemical markers.
missing_descriptors: Commonly documented notes absent from this short card include rose petals/oil, strawberry and other red berries, cherry, plum, basil/spice, honey and sometimes candied citrus; exact profiles depend strongly on dry versus sweet style.
editor_conclusion: Keep aromatic intensity as a cultivar trait; present dehydration as one possible modifier, not the sole cause or preservation rationale.

comparison: CEVVIN places the largest Serbian commercial Bagrina area in Negotinska Krajina and documents preservation there. wein.plus and genetics show a wider Romania–Serbia–Banat/Balkan identity, so Negotin is the Serbian stronghold, not proof of exclusive origin.
independence: National register/profile, specialist lexicon and peer-reviewed genetics converge on local importance plus wider history.
missing_definition: Distinguish present Serbian stronghold, traditional range and genetic/geographic origin.
editor_conclusion: Keep Negotin as the principal Serbian association, with the wider regional-history caveat.

comparison: Crvena Dinka/Červená Dinka is listed among Bagrina synonyms by public wein.plus and is consistent with the Braghina Rosie identity confirmed by genetics.
independence: Specialist synonymy and genetic identity align, although the genetic paper does not independently test every vernacular name.
missing_definition: Preserve diacritics and note that a synonym is not a separate cultivar unless a specific accession differs genetically.
editor_conclusion: Keep Crvena Dinka as a documented synonym.

comparison: CEVVIN and the current SerbianWine.rs page directly describe reddish berries while classifying Bagrina as a white wine cultivar. No audited source ranks their darkness against all other white cultivars.
independence: CEVVIN, wein.plus, peer-reviewed genetics and the corrected current SerbianWine.rs page agree on the white cultivar with reddish skins.
missing_definition: Use a colour chart or OIV berry-skin code for a comparative darkness claim; otherwise simply say reddish berries.
editor_conclusion: Keep «reddish skin» and remove the undefined comparison.

comparison: Pear was not found in the accessible Matalj vintage notes, CEVVIN profile/monograph summary, specialist databases or independent reporting.
independence: The checked product and research corpora are silent rather than contradictory.
missing_definition: Supply a dated wine/vintage and original tasting source if pear is retained.
editor_conclusion: Remove pear from the generic/Matalj line until a traceable source is added.

comparison: Melon was not found in the accessible Matalj vintage notes, CEVVIN profile/monograph summary, specialist databases or independent reporting.
independence: The checked product and research corpora are silent rather than contradictory.
missing_definition: Supply a dated wine/vintage and original tasting source if melon is retained.
editor_conclusion: Remove melon until a traceable source is added.

comparison: Apricot repeats across several Matalj vintages and is compatible with the broader fruit family in the experimental set. Evidence is strongest for Matalj, not every Bagrina.
independence: Multiple pages mostly reproduce producer copy; the research corpus independently supports fruit generally, not apricot specifically in every sample.
editor_conclusion: Keep apricot under explicit Matalj attribution or as a possible descriptor.

comparison: Fresh quince is repeated in Matalj Bagrina Bukovska notes but not isolated as a cultivar-wide marker in the 21-sample summary.
independence: Repeated retail text is source-dependent on one producer; broader research confirms fruit variation.
editor_conclusion: Keep fresh quince only within the Matalj profile.

comparison: Hay repeats across Matalj vintages, while CEVVIN's wider work reports herbal notes in some samples without making hay universal.
independence: Producer-derived repetition plus broader experimental herbal context give partial independence.
editor_conclusion: Keep hay as a Matalj/occasional descriptor.

comparison: Field flowers are explicit in Matalj notes and the scientific panel independently reports floral aromas as a dominant family, though not that exact flower term in every sample.
independence: Bottle-specific and experimental evidence converge at family level.
editor_conclusion: Keep field flowers within Matalj; use «floral» for the broad cultivar range.

comparison: Rosemary is traceable to Matalj Bagrina descriptions but not to a cross-producer or experimental consensus.
independence: Visible repetitions appear textually dependent on producer copy.
editor_conclusion: Attribute rosemary to Matalj, not the cultivar generally.

comparison: Sage recurs in several Matalj vintages and fits the experimental herbal family, but is primarily a producer-specific descriptor.
independence: Vintage notes and general experimental herbal evidence overlap only at family level.
editor_conclusion: Keep sage under Matalj attribution.

comparison: Chamomile is repeated in Matalj-derived product text but not independently established across producers or the experimental summary.
independence: Retail repetitions likely share one source.
editor_conclusion: Attribute chamomile to Matalj only.

comparison: Mango is explicit in selected Matalj vintages and fits the experimental tropical-fruit family. No evidence ties its appearance specifically to objectively «successful» years.
independence: Producer/vintage evidence and experimental family-level evidence converge, but the vintage-quality causal rule is unsupported.
missing_definition: Define successful year by harvest/quality metrics rather than descriptor presence.
editor_conclusion: Keep mango as a vintage-specific Matalj note; remove «in successful years» unless defined.

comparison: Jasmine appears in selected Matalj vintages and in separate Serbian specialist coverage of Bagrina's floral character; the 21-sample set remains variable.
independence: Producer-derived notes and independent media support occurrence, not universality.
editor_conclusion: Keep jasmine as an occasional/Matalj descriptor.

comparison: White tea is visible in selected Matalj commercial descriptions but has no independent cultivar-wide confirmation.
independence: Multiple store pages appear to reproduce the same producer note.
editor_conclusion: Attribute white tea to the named Matalj vintage.

comparison: Barrique ageing is reported for some Matalj vintages while others use steel, but the accessible notes do not consistently state a light toast aroma. The scientific microvinifications reportedly had no wood influence.
independence: Technology varies by vintage; no independent tasting consistently confirms toast.
missing_definition: Name vintage, vessel, new-oak share, toast level and tasting source.
editor_conclusion: Do not append generic toast; attribute it only to a sourced barrel-aged vintage.

comparison: Matalj vintages are described from moderately full to full, matching the stated range. The experimental wines vary enough that this should remain a style range, not a cultivar constant.
independence: Different vintage pages agree on the range; CEVVIN independently supports structural variability.
missing_definition: Body is sensory and should be linked to alcohol, extract and vintage where possible.
editor_conclusion: Keep the range under Matalj attribution.

comparison: Creamy texture is explicit in selected Matalj vintages but not a common property of all 21 experimental wines.
independence: Evidence is producer/vintage-specific.
missing_definition: Name vintage and élevage, because lees work, oak and malolactic conversion may affect creaminess.
editor_conclusion: Attribute creaminess to selected Matalj vintages.

comparison: Matalj notes explicitly link minerality to a firm, tense or dynamic palate sensation. The research average found mineral tones weak, and the term does not prove literal soil-mineral transfer.
independence: Producer wording is clear; experimental evidence qualifies its typicality.
missing_definition: Define minerality operationally as a sensory impression and avoid geological causation.
editor_conclusion: Keep as an attributed sensory metaphor, not a universal or chemical fact.

comparison: The detailed two-part profile maps to different Matalj vintage descriptions: 2021-style apricot/quince/herbs and 2020/2024-style mango/jasmine/white tea, with changing body and élevage.
independence: Traceability is high, but the texts are producer-derived and not independent varietal consensus.
missing_definition: Name the relevant vintage beside each descriptor set so readers do not read the merged list as one bottle or universal profile.
editor_conclusion: Keep the Matalj attribution and split the descriptors by vintage/style.

comparison: CEVVIN's publication catalogue and Serbian research metadata confirm Sorta vinove loze Bagrina, Niš 2023, edited by Darko Jakšić, ISBN 978-86-912489-3-2.
independence: Official catalogue, national research repository metadata and contemporary specialist reporting agree bibliographically.
editor_conclusion: Keep the monograph citation and add full bibliographic data.

comparison: The programme inspected 13,110 vines, selected 21 plants/genotypes and evaluated microvinifications with CEVVIN, CREA-VE Asti and local participants. «About two dozen» is acceptable rounding, but 21 is available and preferable.
independence: The monograph and an on-site specialist report converge on the design and sample count.
missing_definition: Separate the 21 microvinifications from the six labelled market wines also tasted by the local group.
editor_conclusion: Use the exact 21 and distinguish scientific and local-panel sample sets.

comparison: Apple appears in the monograph's broader experimental descriptor set, while public reporting summarises fresh fruit rather than making apple universal.
independence: Direct monograph evidence is primary; public report corroborates the family only.
editor_conclusion: Keep as one observed microvinification descriptor.

comparison: Peach appears in the monograph's broader set, consistent with fresh/ripe fruit but not present in every sample.
independence: Direct monograph evidence is primary; public report corroborates fruit dominance.
editor_conclusion: Keep as one observed descriptor, not a universal marker.

comparison: The scientific panel found floral aromas among the dominant families, and Matalj plus separate Serbian coverage supply concrete floral examples.
independence: Experimental, producer and specialist-media evidence converge.
missing_descriptors: Specific flowers documented elsewhere include field flowers, jasmine and honeysuckle-like notes.
editor_conclusion: Keep flowers as a well-supported descriptor family.

comparison: Honey was observed in the experimental/local sensory material but only in part of the set; the scientific average and local panel differed in emphasis.
independence: Monograph evidence and public event reporting agree on occurrence, not universality.
editor_conclusion: Keep «sometimes honey».

comparison: Mint is present in the monograph descriptor range but is not prominent in the public aggregate report or producer consensus.
independence: Direct research source supports occurrence; external corroboration is limited.
editor_conclusion: Keep only as an occasional experimental note.

comparison: Spice occurred in some samples, while the scientific-panel average reportedly rated spicy tones minor relative to fruit and flowers.
independence: The monograph and public report agree on presence with low aggregate prominence.
editor_conclusion: Keep «sometimes spice», not a dominant cultivar signature.

comparison: The public project report explicitly contrasts lower- and higher-acid samples and links the differences to wine harmony; the monograph provides the detailed set.
independence: Direct research and on-site reporting converge.
missing_definition: Separate laboratory total acidity/pH from sensory sourness.
editor_conclusion: Keep sample-to-sample acidity variation.

comparison: Bitterness variation is reported in the monograph, but the public specialist report does not discuss it as explicitly as acidity and aroma.
independence: Primary evidence is direct but public independent corroboration is limited.
missing_definition: Report the sensory scale, panel and sample values if bitterness becomes an editorial conclusion.
editor_conclusion: Keep as a monograph-attributed finding.

comparison: The 21 selected genotypes and wines ranged from near-neutral to strongly aromatic and differed in acidity, structure and finish; even labelled wines differed. Because selection intentionally sought diversity, «very variable» is valid for the studied material but not proof that every commercial bottle is unstable.
independence: Monograph, on-site report and changing Matalj vintage profiles converge on substantial variation.
missing_definition: Specify genetic, vintage, site and vinification sources of variation rather than treating all as one cultivar essence.
missing_descriptors: The research aggregate adds citrus, tropical fruit, herbal and occasional smoky impressions beyond the short list; spice and mineral tones were low on one scientific average.
editor_conclusion: Keep high variability with the clonal-selection/sample-scope caveat.

comparison: CEVVIN, peer-reviewed genetics and a Serbian expert interview independently place Začinak chiefly in eastern Serbia and especially Negotinska Krajina/Timok.
independence: National register data, SSR research and expert reporting converge.
missing_definition: Distinguish the Serbian stronghold from an unproved exclusive origin.
editor_conclusion: Keep Negotin/Negotinska Krajina as the principal association.

comparison: Historical Šumadija/Oplenac lists include Začinak, but current CEVVIN commercial data name Negotinska Krajina and Tri Morave as the largest concentrations and record only 0.08 ha nationally.
independence: Historical tourism/royal-vineyard lists and current register data address different periods.
missing_definition: Label Šumadija as historical presence unless a current registered planting is supplied.
editor_conclusion: Do not present Šumadija as a current stronghold; use «historically recorded» or replace with Tri Morave in a current-distribution tag.

comparison: CEVVIN and the Yugoslav manual directly classify Začinak as bojadiser because its must is partly/fully coloured; generic English, German and Russian Wikipedia definitions agree that teinturiers contain pigment beyond the skin and are used to deepen colour.
independence: Current national technical data, historical manual, specialist lexicon and generic encyclopaedic definitions converge.
missing_definition: A bojadiser/teinturier has anthocyanins in flesh/must as well as skin; «partly coloured» is more precise for Začinak than implying an opaque red juice.
missing_descriptors: CEVVIN adds high extract and a dark red-black wine profile.
editor_conclusion: Keep «красильный сорт» and define it through partly coloured must.

comparison: wein.plus lists Krajinsko Crno as a Začinak synonym, but no independent source in the selected corpus establishes it as the ordinary name of a monovarietal wine.
independence: The assertion depends on one broad synonym compilation and is not reproduced by CEVVIN or the genetic study.
missing_definition: Separate cultivar synonym, wine label and regional style name.
editor_conclusion: If retained, call Krajinsko Crno a lexicon-listed cultivar synonym, not a proven local wine name.

comparison: Negotinsko Crno is not an unambiguous name for wine made from Začinak alone. CEVVIN and a Croatian register use it as a Začinak synonym, English/German Wikipedia assign it to Prokupac, and Serbian specialist reporting uses it for the historical Prokupac–Začinak–Kadarka blend.
independence: Official registers, Wikipedia synonym lists, genetics warnings and multiple modern reports expose the collision.
missing_definition: State whether the term denotes a local cultivar accession, Prokupac synonym in an older database, or the traditional field blend.
editor_conclusion: In wine context define Negotinsko crno as the historical three-variety blend; do not present it as a simple monovarietal Začinak name.

comparison: Crno means black/dark, so «краинское чёрное» and «неготинское чёрное» are semantic Russian translations. «Неготинско црно» preserves Serbian morphology and is a Cyrillic transliteration, not a Russian translation.
independence: Basic Serbian–Russian linguistic correspondence is stable; the factual problem lies in the underlying ambiguous wine/cultivar name.
missing_definition: Label translation and transliteration separately.
editor_conclusion: Use two Russian translations consistently or preserve both Serbian originals unchanged and explain their ambiguous use.

comparison: The official Matalj 2017 page documents a 100% Začinak wine, and specialist reporting records rare experimental monovarietal releases.
independence: Producer documentation and independent reporting converge on existence and rarity.
missing_definition: Name producer and vintage because availability is intermittent.
editor_conclusion: Keep that monovarietal Začinak exists, with explicit vintage attribution.

comparison: Matalj's technical page explicitly identifies Začinak Bukovski 2017 as 100% Začinak, 13.0% alcohol and 1.2 g/L residual sugar.
independence: Primary product evidence is exact; independent sources confirm the producer and rare-variety project but not every number.
missing_definition: Attach the 2017 vintage so the note is not confused with later Bukovski Cuvée blends.
missing_descriptors: Muted purple colour; mint; concentrated fresh nose; polished tannins; lively acids; light chocolate; moderately long fruity finish.
editor_conclusion: Keep the named wine and add 2017/100% to prevent confusion with Bukovski Cuvée.

comparison: Sour cherry is exact in the official 2017 Matalj note, but no cross-producer corpus makes it universal for Začinak.
independence: The direct source is producer-authored and bottle-specific.
editor_conclusion: Keep under explicit Matalj 2017 attribution.

comparison: Pomegranate is exact in the official Matalj 2017 note, without independent cultivar-wide confirmation.
independence: Single primary producer note.
editor_conclusion: Keep under explicit Matalj 2017 attribution.

comparison: Blueberry is exact in the official Matalj 2017 note, without independent proof that it recurs across Začinak wines.
independence: Single primary producer note.
editor_conclusion: Keep under explicit Matalj 2017 attribution.

comparison: The producer calls the 2017 palate soft and the tannins persistent but highly polished. Traditional technical profiles permit some astringency, so softness belongs to this bottle rather than every Začinak.
independence: Producer and national profile address different styles and scopes.
missing_definition: Softness is sensory balance, not absence of tannin.
missing_descriptors: Persistent, polished tannins balanced with lively acids.
editor_conclusion: Keep «soft» for Matalj 2017 only.

comparison: Moderately full body is exact for Matalj 2017; it should not be converted into a universal varietal rule.
independence: Producer-specific direct evidence; broad independent body data are absent.
missing_definition: Body depends on alcohol, extract, yield and vinification.
editor_conclusion: Keep under the named bottle/vintage.

comparison: Matalj explicitly describes fresh aroma and palate with lively acids, while the national profile's total-acidity range is compatible but not a sensory guarantee.
independence: Producer note and technical profile converge at different levels.
missing_definition: Separate measured total acidity from perceived freshness.
missing_descriptors: Lively acids in balance with polished tannins.
editor_conclusion: Keep freshness as an attributed 2017 descriptor.

comparison: The producer explicitly calls the 2017 palate and finish fruity; the named aroma fruits are sour cherry, pomegranate and blueberry.
independence: Direct but producer-authored bottle note.
missing_descriptors: Mint and light chocolate broaden the producer's profile beyond fruit.
editor_conclusion: Keep under explicit Matalj 2017 attribution.

comparison: CEVVIN states that Začinak must is partly coloured and the historical manual calls its juice coloured. That is the technical reason it can be called bojadiser; «light juice» contradicts the same paragraph's cultivar classification.
independence: Current national profile, historical manual and generic Wikipedia/wein.plus teinturier definitions converge.
missing_definition: Partly coloured must need not be as dark as the finished wine, but it is not equivalent to the colourless juice of an ordinary red cultivar.
editor_conclusion: Correct «light juice» to «partly coloured must».

comparison: Maceration can extract additional pigment from skins, but Začinak already carries pigment in the must. No audited Začinak source gives a universal long-maceration protocol, and the Matalj 2017 page gives no maceration duration.
independence: Ampelographic and generic technical sources refute the sole-source mechanism; product evidence is silent on duration.
missing_definition: Distinguish pigment already in crushed must from additional skin extraction during maceration.
editor_conclusion: Remove the sole-cause claim and do not state long maceration without a dated technical sheet.

comparison: CEVVIN, the historical manual and wein.plus consistently describe intensely coloured wine; Matalj 2017 specifies a muted purple shade.
independence: National, historical, specialist and producer sources converge.
missing_definition: Colour intensity and hue are different dimensions; attach muted purple only to 2017.
editor_conclusion: Keep the deep-colour statement.

comparison: Some astringency is documented, but CEVVIN says slight and Matalj 2017 reports well-polished tannins. The broad word «astringent» can imply more severity than the evidence.
independence: National technical and producer evidence converge on tannin presence while differing in expression.
missing_definition: Separate tannin amount, grain/texture and sensory astringency.
missing_descriptors: Matalj: persistent, highly polished tannins.
editor_conclusion: Use «slightly astringent in traditional profiles; polished in Matalj 2017» rather than an absolute.

comparison: CEVVIN reports 6–7 g/L total acidity and Matalj reports lively acidity; neither means every bottle tastes sour.
independence: Measured national profile and bottle-specific sensory note agree on meaningful acidity.
missing_definition: Total acidity is chemical; sourness is a sensory balance involving pH, fruit, alcohol, tannin and residual sugar.
editor_conclusion: Replace «sourish» with «can retain lively/notable acidity» or give the analytical range.

comparison: Varietal Začinak is demonstrably rare, but CEVVIN's 0.08 ha total area and the historical role as a blending grape explain scarcity at least as strongly as colour, tannin or acidity. Matalj 2017 shows those traits do not prevent a balanced varietal wine.
independence: Register data, technical history, producer bottle and independent reporting converge on rarity but not the book's single causal chain.
missing_definition: Separate planting scarcity, commercial availability and sensory suitability.
editor_conclusion: Keep rarity; remove «so much that» or list multiple causes.

comparison: CEVVIN, the historical manual, wein.plus, generic Wikipedia definitions and modern blends all document colour-strengthening use.
independence: Multiple independent technical, historical and commercial sources converge.
missing_definition: Colour addition can be one goal among structure, acidity and local-style restoration.
editor_conclusion: Keep blending for colour.

comparison: German Wikipedia says teinturiers generally form under 5% in colour-correction blends, and the old manual says small additions. But the important modern Bukovski Cuvée examples contain about 25–30% Začinak, and no representative dataset establishes what is «usual» specifically for this cultivar.
independence: Generic technical tradition and dated Začinak recipes describe different use cases rather than a single distribution.
missing_definition: State the exact wine/vintage and purpose before giving a percentage.
editor_conclusion: Remove «usually single-digit» as a Začinak-wide rule; cite 25% for Bukovski Cuvée 2021 if an example is wanted.

comparison: Mint is explicit in the complete official Matalj 2017 note and omitted only by the shortened book summary.
independence: Primary direct evidence; independent recurrence is not claimed.
editor_conclusion: Add mint only to the Matalj 2017 descriptor set.

comparison: The official note describes a very fresh, forceful and highly concentrated nose. These are producer sensory judgements for one vintage, not measured cultivar constants.
independence: Single direct producer source.
missing_definition: If «concentrated» is retained, label it as aroma intensity, not analytically measured extract.
editor_conclusion: Optional bottle-specific addition under Matalj 2017 attribution.

comparison: Persistent, very well-polished tannins are explicit in the official 2017 note.
independence: Primary direct evidence; no universal claim is made.
missing_definition: Polished describes texture/quality, not low tannin concentration.
editor_conclusion: Add to the Matalj 2017 profile if structural detail is desired.

comparison: The producer explicitly balances lively acids against polished tannins, a more faithful account of the 2017 palate than generic sourness.
independence: Primary direct evidence; compatible with CEVVIN's analytical acidity range.
missing_definition: Perceived balance is sensory; total acidity remains a separate measurement.
editor_conclusion: Prefer this attributed balance description for the named wine.

comparison: A light chocolate note is explicit in the 2017 finish, but no source shows it as a recurring cultivar marker or identifies whether it derives from oak or bottle age.
independence: Single producer note.
missing_definition: Do not assign a technological cause without an élevage record.
editor_conclusion: Add only as a light Matalj 2017 finish note.

comparison: The official note explicitly calls the finish fruity and moderately long.
independence: Primary direct evidence; no universal claim is made.
editor_conclusion: Optional bottle-specific addition.

comparison: CEVVIN explicitly gives 18–22% sugar and 7–9 g/L total acidity in must and calls the must partly coloured.
independence: Current national technical source; the historical manual independently agrees on coloured juice.
missing_definition: Specify whether sugar is mass percentage/soluble-solids convention and retain the source's approximate range.
editor_conclusion: Use these values as an attributed technical profile, especially to correct the light-juice error.

comparison: CEVVIN gives the complete traditional wine profile: 10–11% alcohol, 6–7 g/L total acidity, much extract, red-black colour and slight astringency. Matalj 2017 at 13% demonstrates that modern examples can depart from those typical values.
independence: National technical profile and actual producer wine converge on style but show vintage/production variation.
missing_definition: Label CEVVIN values as typical/traditional, not legal limits or universal bottle specifications.
editor_conclusion: Useful as an attributed technical baseline; do not overwrite the separate 2017 product data.

comparison: wein.plus calls Začinak wines spicy, matching the variety's name and broad blending reputation, but the official Matalj 2017 note does not foreground spice and no multiwine sensory study quantifies it.
independence: Specialist lexicon support exists; producer bottle evidence is not confirmatory.
missing_definition: Treat spice as a possible broad descriptor, not a universal marker or an etymological proof.
editor_conclusion: List as a possible specialist-lexicon descriptor with source attribution.

comparison: CEVVIN's register-based profile reports just 0.08 ha and rank 78 in Serbian commercial vineyards, directly quantifying extreme rarity.
independence: Authoritative current register analysis; qualitative rarity is independently echoed by expert and wine-press sources.
missing_definition: Commercial registered area excludes every unregistered household or conservation vine and must be dated.
editor_conclusion: Add the dated 0.08 ha figure when explaining scarcity.

comparison: No selected grape authority or requested Wikipedia records Temišvarka for Kreaca, while targeted public searches consistently return Acorus calamus or unrelated demonyms/toponyms.
independence: CEVVIN, VIVC-derived lists, peer-reviewed papers, wein.plus and all six Wikipedias independently fail to support the grape synonym; botanical usage supplies a positive competing meaning.
missing_definition: An undocumented household nickname remains logically possible, but it cannot be printed as an established synonym without a primary ampelographic source.
editor_conclusion: Remove «темишварка» from the Kreaca heading unless a traceable viticultural source is produced; do not infer it merely from proximity to Timișoara.

comparison: English and German Wikipedia, CEVVIN, wein.plus, scientific literature and VIVC-derived catalogues consistently identify Kreaca as a white Vitis vinifera cultivar.
independence: Multiple national, international, scientific and encyclopaedic sources converge.
missing_definition: German Wikipedia also flags possible table-grape use; the book's wine context remains correct.
editor_conclusion: Keep «белая».

comparison: Serbian science supports autochthonous Banat status, CEVVIN uses autochthonous/regional Balkan, and wein.plus says Balkan origin. Current area and clone work strongly tie it to South Banat, Vršac and Gudurica but not exclusively to the city.
independence: Peer-reviewed, national-centre and international specialist sources converge on the broader region.
missing_definition: Distinguish geographic emblematic association from proven place of first origin.
editor_conclusion: Replace the compressed formula with «автохтонный/региональный белый сорт Баната, особенно связанный с Вршацем и Гудурицей».

comparison: CEVVIN explicitly calls the berry neutral in taste; the peer-reviewed clone paper independently says the colourless mesocarp is soft, juicy and neutral.
independence: Current national technical and peer-reviewed scientific descriptions agree.
missing_definition: Neutral berry taste concerns the grape flesh/must and does not mean the finished wine has no aroma.
missing_descriptors: The berry is also described as soft and juicy.
editor_conclusion: Keep neutral berry, with the grape-versus-wine distinction.

comparison: CEVVIN, the 1964 Serbian manual and Croatian Vinopedia say late or third-epoch ripening; Vinograd.info says early-middle or middle ripening.
independence: Three regionally grounded sources converge against one Russian secondary profile whose primary basis is unclear.
missing_definition: Ripening epochs are relative to local climate and reference cultivars, so cross-country labels are not automatically identical.
editor_conclusion: Retain «позднее» under explicit CEVVIN attribution and footnote the conflicting Russian profile if exhaustive transparency is desired.

comparison: CEVVIN directly says lower sugar accumulation. Historical typical must was 18–20%, while the clone study ranged 17.6–22.6% across clone means and 18.7–20.8% by year.
independence: National technical, historical manual and measured peer-reviewed results align on moderate typical values while documenting variation.
missing_definition: «Comparatively little» needs its comparison class and is not a fixed analytical ceiling.
missing_descriptors: Include measured ranges only with dates, site and study design.
editor_conclusion: Keep the source-attributed comparative wording; do not paraphrase it as inherently low-Brix every year.

comparison: CEVVIN and the historical manual use the same harmonious-wine descriptor, reinforced by regional reporting.
independence: Current technical, historical and public-regional sources converge.
missing_definition: Harmonious is a sensory judgement of balance, not a chemical measurement.
editor_conclusion: Keep «гармоничное».

comparison: Drinkable/easy-drinking is repeated by CEVVIN, the historical manual and RTV's local report.
independence: Current, historical and regional sources converge.
missing_definition: Pitko means readily drinkable/approachable, not automatically simple or low quality.
editor_conclusion: Keep «питкое», preferably with a short definition for Russian readers.

comparison: CEVVIN's exact category is mass wines of better quality. The 1964 manual likewise places Kreaca among weaker whites but explicitly rates it above Plovdina, Ružica and Slankamenka.
independence: Current and historical Serbian technical taxonomies agree on large-volume/table orientation while resisting a simplistic poor-quality gloss.
missing_definition: Mass wine is a production/market category and should not be equated with defective, neutral or industrially adulterated wine.
editor_conclusion: Retain only as «исторически относилась к группе массовых вин лучшего качества».

comparison: English and German Wikipedia, wein.plus, VIVC-derived lists, the 1983 regulation, the clone paper and regional sources all document Banatski/Banat/Bánáti Rizling forms as Kreaca names.
