comparison: Local cultivars are credibly linked to genetic resources, authenticity and regional identity, but «интереснее» is a declared preference and no source can objectively show that they explain regional character better than international cultivars grown under the same terroir and practices.
independence: The peer-reviewed local-variety study and producer association independently establish conservation and identity relevance; Wikipedia and register statistics cannot adjudicate comparative interest or explanatory power.
missing_definition: An objective comparison would require defined sensory, cultural, genetic or market criteria for «interesting» and «explains the region».
missing_descriptors: The sentence does not mark the judgment as the book's editorial principle.
editor_conclusion: Retain as a transparent authorial thesis: «для этой книги автохтонные и давно местные сорта важнее как проводники региональной истории»; do not present comparative interest as a statistical finding.

comparison: All six requested Wikipedias, VIVC-linked nomenclature, current Serbian guidance and specialist genetics agree that Grašac/Grašac Beli, Graševina, Italian Riesling/Riesling Italico and Welschriesling denote the same cultivar and that it is not Rhine Riesling.
independence: International catalogue tradition, multilingual encyclopedias, genetic research and Serbian regional guidance converge on identity and non-relationship.
missing_definition: Name use varies by country and label; synonymy does not make Grašac the preferred legal name in every jurisdiction.
editor_conclusion: Keep the synonym set and the explicit warning that Rhine Riesling is a different cultivar.

comparison: The cultivar is internationally distributed and not a uniquely Serbian genotype, while the documented nineteenth-century Grašac name, centuries of local cultivation and modern Fruška Gora identity support «domestic in practice» as cultural history. No named source for the exact quotation «он у нас дома» or a collective of oenologists was found.
independence: Genetic and multilingual sources establish international identity; historical and current Serbian specialist sources independently establish long local domestication and regional ownership.
missing_definition: Separate genetic origin, international distribution, legal cultivar category and cultural domestication; name any quoted oenologist.
missing_descriptors: The modern Serbian heartland is Fruška Gora/Srem, but the cultivar is planted nationally and across neighbouring countries.
editor_conclusion: Write «международно распространённый сорт, веками свой для Фрушки горы»; remove quotation marks or attribute the words to a named speaker and source.

comparison: A dated 2017 article repeats an older more-than-half estimate for Fruška Gora, but the Vršac figure found in the corpus is the assortment share of Vršački vinogradi, not the share of all regional vineyard land. No current register verifies the same present-tense threshold in both regions.
independence: The Fruška line is a peer-reviewed secondary citation; the Vršac line is a winery profile with a different denominator. Their numbers cannot be combined into one regional claim.
missing_definition: The text needs a year, territorial boundary and denominator for each region: planted hectares, registered commercial parcels, estate assortment or grape purchases.
missing_descriptors: Current official national data do not provide the required two regional cultivar tables.
editor_conclusion: Remove the combined claim. If retained, separate it into «an older estimate put Fruška Gora above half» and «Italian Riesling exceeded half of the historical Vršački vinogradi assortment».

comparison: Named Serbian professionals and current specialist syntheses document the return to the Grašac name, increased quality attention, site selection, diverse vinification and major international recognition. This is a clear reputational and stylistic revival.
independence: GuildSomm, The Buyer, Serbian specialist reporting and named producer examples converge, although interview testimony supplies some market details.
missing_definition: The revival concerns name, reputation, quality ambitions and style diversity; the cultivar itself never disappeared from Serbian vineyards.
missing_descriptors: Stainless, sur lie, barrel, sparkling, skin-contact, sweet and age-worthy examples illustrate the change.
editor_conclusion: Keep «переживает возрождение», preferably as «переживает качественное и репутационное возрождение».

comparison: German Wikipedia and current Serbian wines support pale green-yellow, light yellow, straw and gold appearances across age and concentration. «Straw-yellow» is plausible but narrower than the observed range.
independence: Generic encyclopedic profile and several named Serbian product or tasting records agree on a pale-to-golden spectrum.
missing_definition: Colour depends on age, ripeness, oxidation, skin contact and vessel; it is not fixed by cultivar identity.
missing_descriptors: Young examples often have green reflections; mature or concentrated versions become more golden.
editor_conclusion: Write «обычно светло-жёлтый, нередко с зеленоватым оттенком; с возрастом и концентрацией золотистее».

comparison: Dry still Grašac is common and well documented, but encyclopedic and specialist sources also show off-dry, sweet, botrytised, ice, sparkling and skin-contact wines.
independence: Multilingual reference sources and named Serbian producers independently demonstrate the dry core style and broader range.
missing_definition: «Dry» is a wine's residual-sugar category, not a permanent property of the grape.
missing_descriptors: The card should signal whether it describes a typical young dry style or the full varietal range.
editor_conclusion: Change the opening to «в типичной молодой сухой версии» or explicitly add the other styles.

comparison: Recognisable fruit, floral and herbal families are supported, but current Serbian guidance says the grape's value lies in versatility rather than one dramatic aroma, The Buyer calls its aromas delicate, and specialist history records a former reputation for neutrality. «Pronounced varietal aroma» is not a safe generic rule.
independence: German Wikipedia, GuildSomm, SerbianWine.rs, professional reporting and named wines converge on a real but variable aromatic range.
missing_definition: Aroma intensity and varietal specificity are separate: a wine may be aromatic without having a unique diagnostic marker.
missing_descriptors: Yield, ripeness, clone, site, lees, oak, skin contact and age materially change the aromatic profile.
editor_conclusion: Replace with «от деликатного до выраженного аромата в зависимости от участка и винификации».

comparison: Green or yellow apple and citrus recur in German Wikipedia, the current Serbian guide, GuildSomm, aroma-research synthesis and multiple named Serbian wines.
independence: Encyclopedic, specialist, scientific and wine-level evidence converge on these core families.
missing_descriptors: Citrus may appear as lemon, lime, grapefruit or zest; pear, white flowers, herbs and hay are common companions.
editor_conclusion: Keep citrus and green apple as typical, not mandatory, descriptors.

comparison: Croatian regional material, GuildSomm and current Serbian guidance all report slight or gently bitter finishes. The exact impression ranges from generic savoury bitterness to almond-like bitterness.
independence: Neighbouring regional, international specialist and Serbian current-guide lines converge, while individual wines show variable intensity.
missing_definition: Pleasantness is an evaluative judgment; bitterness level and integration should be tied to a style or wine where possible.
missing_descriptors: Almond, herbs, citrus peel and phenolic grip can overlap perceptually but are not identical.
editor_conclusion: Keep «лёгкая приятная горчинка», marking it as frequent rather than universal.

comparison: The claim about the sources is factually wrong: GuildSomm explicitly writes of slight almond bitterness, and independent Serbian tasting reports also record almond and marzipan notes. Sources do not limit themselves to unnamed pleasant bitterness.
independence: A major specialist synthesis and independent wine-level tasting evidence provide separate almond-related lines.
missing_definition: An almond taste, almond-like bitterness and age-related marzipan aroma are related but distinct observations.
missing_descriptors: Almond is optional and may be more evident in some wines or with age.
editor_conclusion: Replace the meta-comment with «иногда горчинка напоминает миндаль; в других винах она остаётся просто травянистой или цитрусовой».

comparison: The 12–13% zone is well represented among fresh dry wines and generic references describe modest alcohol, but current Cargraš is 13.5% and Vinum's barrel-aged 26A 2020 is 14.5%. The stated 11–13% range omits established stronger styles and is not a cultivar limit.
independence: Several official product specifications and an independent specialist vertical provide wine-level measurements across styles.
missing_definition: State whether the range concerns young dry stainless-steel wines, all Serbian bottlings or physiological potential; ABV varies by ripeness and vinification.
missing_descriptors: Named examples: Erdevik Geronimo 12.5%, Verkat 2023 13%, Imperator Cargraš 13.5%, Vinum 26A 2020 14.5%.
editor_conclusion: Write «молодые сухие версии часто около 12–13%, но концентрированные и бочковые достигают 13.5–14.5%».

comparison: Several current dry-still examples fall within 5–7 g/L, including 5.4, 5.8, 6.14 and 6.5 g/L, so the range is useful for that style. Dina sparkling reaches 7.2 and Verkat 4.0 reaches 7.5 g/L; the range is therefore not universal. Serbian regulation supports expression as tartaric acid.
independence: Official producer analyses, an independent specialist report, a Serbian catalogue entry and the legal analytical convention converge.
missing_definition: Specify wine style, vintage and whether the number is total/titratable acidity expressed as tartaric-acid equivalents; do not confuse it with pH.
missing_descriptors: Observed pH values in named examples include 3.05, 3.10, 3.15, 3.27 and 3.35, showing why acidity and pH should remain separate.
editor_conclusion: Keep 5–7 g/L only as «a common range for young dry still examples» and note that sparkling or selected wines may exceed it.

comparison: The end-2025 commercial Vineyard Register makes Chardonnay Serbia's leading white cultivar and third cultivar overall at 9%. Current guides document it in both northern Vojvodina and multiple central regions, and Decanter calls it one of the international grapes doing particularly well; literal presence in every Serbian district was not established.
independence: A Ministry register, a current multi-region tasting guide and specialist country coverage converge on major national importance and broad distribution.
missing_definition: «One of the pillars» should be tied to a measurable area share, portfolio breadth or award record; «everywhere» must not be read as a cadastral claim about every wine district.
missing_descriptors: The block omits that Chardonnay leads Serbian white cultivars in the end-2025 commercial register and spans still, sparkling, unoaked, barrel-aged and amphora-influenced styles.
editor_conclusion: Keep the prominence claim as «leading white cultivar in the end-2025 commercial register, 9%, and widely represented across regions»; replace literal «повсюду» with «во многих районах».

comparison: Official and independently reproduced DWWA 2026 results show seven Serbian Gold wines. Three are Chardonnay: Tarpoš Chardonnay Extra Brut 2021, Zvonko Bogdan Chardonnay 2022 and Éclater Blanc de Blancs Brut Nature 2018; the Éclater product specification confirms Chardonnay despite the cultivar not appearing in the short label.
independence: The official competition database, Chamber reporting via Tanjug, specialist press and the Éclater producer specification agree on the count and identities.
missing_definition: Count wines, not wineries or medal stickers; identify Éclater as the third Chardonnay and distinguish Gold from the separately promoted Platinum result.
missing_descriptors: Two of the three Gold wines are sparkling: Tarpoš Extra Brut and Éclater Brut Nature; the Zvonko Bogdan Chardonnay 2022 is the still varietal wine.
editor_conclusion: Keep the three-of-seven calculation and list all three wines so readers can verify why Éclater is counted as Chardonnay.

comparison: Decanter's full official Platinum list names Deurić La Rem Chardonnay, Fruška Gora, Srem 2023; Serbian Chamber and specialist reports give the same wine 97 points.
independence: The competition organiser is primary for the medal, while two independent Serbian result lists reproduce the producer, wine, vintage and score.
missing_definition: Platinum is a result for La Rem Chardonnay 2023 at DWWA 2026, not a permanent rank for Deurić or Serbian Chardonnay generally.
missing_descriptors: Competition reporting describes pear, apple, peach, citrus, herbs, youthful freshness, honeyed texture and amphora ageing, while the current guide independently emphasizes minerality, salinity, citrus, green apple and pear.
editor_conclusion: Keep the separate Platinum line but print the full identity: «Deurić La Rem Chardonnay 2023 — Platinum DWWA 2026, 97».

comparison: The north supplies restrained and fresh examples, notably La Rem 2023 and Rajić 2023, but the same 2026 guide describes Grumen Chardonnay Selekcija 2024 from Fruška Gora as full, generous, ripe and 14.5%, and Picus Selection as broad, creamy and weighty. The northern corpus is stylistically diverse rather than uniformly cool or restrained.
independence: A current multi-region tasting guide supplies consistently formatted named examples; general cultivar references independently explain why climate and cellar choices both influence Chardonnay style.
missing_definition: «Cool» could mean climate classification, serving temperature, acidity, alcohol or sensory impression. A regional rule requires a defined sample and comparable vintages and winemaking.
missing_descriptors: Northern examples span green apple, citrus, pear, salinity and bright acidity through ripe melon, peach, tropical fruit, cream, toffee and broad texture.
editor_conclusion: Replace the regional rule with examples: «на севере встречаются и точные свежие, и полнотелые бочковые версии».

comparison: Šumadija includes ripe, broad Chardonnays such as opulent Aberdar and very ripe 14.5% Savić 2022, but also bright 12% sparkling Trijumf and precise, acidity-driven Camille 2024. Northern Serbia likewise contains ripe full-bodied examples, so the available corpus does not validate a categorical north-versus-Šumadija ranking.
independence: The same current guide compares named wines across both regions, reducing source-method differences, while encyclopedic material confirms Chardonnay's sensitivity to climate and winemaking without supplying a Serbian binary.
missing_definition: «Denser» and «riper» need measurable proxies such as alcohol, extract, harvest chemistry, body scores or a blinded regional sample; oak and malolactic fermentation can imitate a climate effect.
missing_descriptors: Šumadija examples include ripe pineapple and peach, butter, nougat, caramel, cream and broad texture, but also green apple, citrus, focused acidity, minerality and salinity.
editor_conclusion: Present Šumadija's ripe and barrel-aged wines as examples, not as a region-wide contrast; state that producer, vintage and cellar choices currently explain much of the observed range.

comparison: Current national directories and a multi-region guide document Sauvignon Blanc in both Šumadija and Fruška Gora, while the commercial register-derived guide gives it a substantial 5% national share. The same corpus also records the cultivar outside those two regions, so the labels are representative rather than exhaustive.
independence: A national winery directory, current cross-region tasting guide and encyclopedic country-presence references converge; winery entries independently locate named producers in each region.
missing_definition: Clarify whether the two place names denote principal examples, appellations, vineyard-area concentration or the full distribution; the book currently supplies no metric.
missing_descriptors: The cultivar is represented in several other central, northern and southern districts and should not be made to look exclusive to Šumadija and Fruška Gora.
editor_conclusion: Keep both named regions but write «особенно заметен в Шумадии и на Фрушкой горе; встречается и в других районах» and optionally add the end-2024 national share of 5%.

comparison: Named Serbian wines and general cultivar references repeatedly document gooseberry, elder or elderflower and grass. The three terms are valid elements of the Serbian Sauvignon range, but no evidence makes the exact trio mandatory in every bottle; examples also contain citrus, stone fruit and tropical fruit.
independence: Official producer specifications, an official Decanter tasting, a current independent guide and specialist/encyclopedic cultivar references provide separate descriptor evidence.
missing_definition: Distinguish elderflower from elderberry and define whether the sentence means typical possibilities, a modal profile or a universal sensory signature.
missing_descriptors: Common accompanying notes include lime, grapefruit, peach, pineapple, passion fruit, nettle, herbs, green apple and smoke or oak in Fumé styles.
editor_conclusion: Retain the descriptors as a non-exclusive range: «часто встречаются крыжовник, цвет бузины и травянистые тона, наряду с цитрусом и косточковыми фруктами».

comparison: The word «instead» is contradicted by wine-level evidence. Šumadija SoviNoa combines peach with gooseberry and lemongrass, while other Šumadija and farther-south wines combine pineapple or tropical fruit with grass, nettle, lime or gooseberry; Fruška Gora examples likewise combine green and ripe-fruit notes. Šumadija is central rather than an unambiguous definition of «south».
independence: An official Decanter note, current guide entries across several regions and a northern producer specification independently show coexisting green and ripe/yellow descriptors.
missing_definition: Define the boundary of «south», the sampled vintages and whether the proposed shift concerns aroma frequency, ripeness, climate or winemaking; a regional rule requires a controlled comparative sample.
missing_descriptors: Both regional groups span citrus, gooseberry, grass, nettle, apple, peach, pineapple and tropical fruit, while oak can add smoke and spice.
editor_conclusion: Delete the replacement rule and state the evidence-based continuum: «в более спелых версиях к зелёным и цитрусовым тонам добавляются персик, абрикос или тропические фрукты».

comparison: The official winery page and Wines of Serbia directory identify SoviNoa Fumé Blanc as Matijašević Vinogradi's Sauvignon Blanc from Orašac, Šumadija, matured in French oak.
independence: The producer is primary for wine identity and method; the national directory and independent tasting/competition records corroborate the producer-wine-variety link.
missing_definition: Do not merge the barrel-aged Fumé Blanc with the separate SoviNoa bottling; they are distinct products with different treatment and award histories.
missing_descriptors: The Fumé style adds oak, smoke, spice and texture to citrus, peach, tropical fruit and herbal Sauvignon notes.
editor_conclusion: Keep the producer attribution and print the full vintage when discussing a score: «Matijašević SoviNoa Fumé Blanc 2023».

comparison: SoviNoa Fumé Blanc 2023 was the 96-point Top White Wine and the highest-scoring Sauvignon Blanc in Beth Willard's 268-wine Serbia guide, and earlier vintages have official DWWA Gold results. This makes it defensible as a leading example within attributed evaluations, but not as an eternal, objective national best without a stated comparison set.
independence: The guide supplies the comparative 2026 result; specialist reporting independently reproduces it, and Decanter records a separate Gold for an earlier vintage.
missing_definition: «Best» must name assessor, guide, vintage, sample and date. A top result for the 2023 vintage cannot be generalized to every release or all future Serbian Sauvignons.
missing_descriptors: The 2023 guide note emphasizes lime, nettle, florals, rich smoky wood, acidity and a pithy finish; official notes for other vintages add peach, gooseberry and grapefruit.
editor_conclusion: Write «один из ориентиров; SoviNoa Fumé Blanc 2023 — 96 и Top White Wine у Бет Уиллард» rather than an unqualified superlative.

comparison: The 96-point score is explicitly published in Beth Willard's New Europe Wine Guide – Serbia 2026. Official Decanter material instead records SoviNoa Fumé Blanc 2021 at 95 points and DWWA 2023 Gold; the book has conflated the assessor's Decanter/DWWA role with the publisher of her separate guide.
independence: The guide itself, independent Serbian specialist reporting and Decanter's official record distinguish the two scores, vintages and publishers.
missing_definition: Separate Decanter editorial tastings, DWWA competition results and an independent guide authored by a DWWA Co-Chair; professional affiliation is not publication attribution.
missing_descriptors: The correct record is 2023 vintage / 96 / New Europe Wine Guide 2026, versus 2021 vintage / 95 / DWWA 2023 Gold.
editor_conclusion: Replace «96 баллов Decanter» with «96 баллов Бет Уиллард в New Europe Wine Guide – Serbia 2026».

comparison: The source was a guide tasting, not a competition, and its printed distinction was Top White Wine across white varieties, not Best Sauvignon Blanc. The wine was the guide's highest-scoring Sauvignon Blanc, but that derived observation is different from the published category.
independence: The primary guide shows the tasting scope, score table and Top White Wine category, while specialist reporting reproduces the same wording; no cited source prints the claimed competition category.
missing_definition: Distinguish a formally named award category from a rank derived by filtering the score table, and distinguish a guide tasting from a medal competition.
missing_descriptors: The distinction is broader and in one sense stronger than the book says: the wine topped all whites in the guide, not merely its cultivar, but only within that dated sample.
editor_conclusion: Correct to «Top White Wine путеводителя; самое высоко оценённое Sauvignon Blanc в его выборке» and remove «конкурса».

comparison: Current producer and national directory records place Rhine Riesling in all three named areas: a Džervin varietal wine in Knjaževac, regulated and commercial presence around Negotin, and planted/portfolio examples on Fruška Gora.
independence: Official producer declarations, a local tourism authority, a national winery directory and the government zoning study independently cover the three regions.
missing_definition: The list demonstrates presence, not that these are the only or three leading Serbian regions by vineyard area; the book supplies no area or production denominator.
missing_descriptors: Current named examples include Džervin Riesling 2021 in Knjaževac, Riesling at Francuska Vinarija Rogljevo in Negotin and Rhine Riesling at Imperator on Fruška Gora.
editor_conclusion: Keep the three place names as documented examples and avoid implying an exhaustive or area-ranked distribution.

comparison: Scientific, specialist and multilingual encyclopedic sources agree that Grašac is Welschriesling/Italian Riesling and is unrelated to Rhine Riesling. «True Riesling» is a conventional way to disambiguate the latter from grape names containing Riesling, but it is rhetorically loaded if used to devalue Grašac.
independence: Peer-reviewed Serbian genetic work secures the Grašac–Welschriesling identity; independent English, Russian and local-language references separately establish the Rhine Riesling distinction.
missing_definition: «True» should mean the VIVC cultivar Riesling/Rajnski rizling, not «authentic wine» or superior quality; Grašac remains a real, historically important cultivar under a confusing synonym.
missing_descriptors: Rhine Riesling is typically higher-acid, aromatic and ageworthy; Grašac has its own citrus, apple, herbal and gently bitter range, but sensory difference is not the taxonomic proof.
editor_conclusion: Replace with the neutral formulation «рейнский рислинг — отдельный сорт; грашац — это Welschriesling/Italian Riesling и с ним не связан».

comparison: Presence of Rhine Riesling in Negotin is well supported, but no source in the selected corpus compares it systematically with Tamjanika, Chardonnay, Smederevka and every other regional white cultivar or awards it an objective first place.
independence: Regional and regulatory records independently establish presence; neither is a comparative quality study, and the six Wikipedias contain no Negotin ranking.
missing_definition: «Performed better» needs an assessor, vintages, producers, price band and criterion such as blind scores, medals, consistency, acidity retention or commercial success.
missing_descriptors: The book gives no named Negotin Riesling bottle or tasting note by which readers could evaluate the preference.
editor_conclusion: Retain only as explicitly attributed authorial judgment—«по авторской дегустационной оценке»—or delete until a defined comparative tasting is cited.

comparison: The current producer declaration is unambiguous: Dubravka Gold 2024 is 50% Italian Riesling and 50% Sauvignon Blanc. Rhine Riesling occurs instead in the separate varietal Riesling 2021 and in basic Dubravka 2024 at 30% alongside Italian Riesling.
independence: The producer gives exact varieties and percentages; independent specialist and retail records corroborate a Riesling/Sauvignon Gold blend but abbreviate the Riesling name, explaining how the conflation arose.
missing_definition: Always name the vintage and distinguish Riesling/Rajnski rizling from Italian Riesling/Grašac; also distinguish Dubravka, Dubravka Gold and the varietal Riesling label.
missing_descriptors: Current Dubravka Gold is 12.5% and dry; the product composition, rather than a generic «Riesling» shorthand, determines the cultivar claim.
editor_conclusion: Delete the Rhine Riesling–Gold link. Write instead «Džervin makes a varietal Rhine Riesling; Dubravka Gold 2024 is Italian Riesling + Sauvignon Blanc».

comparison: University registry data and several multilingual cultivar articles converge that Burgundac beli/Beli burgundac is Pinot Blanc and Burgundac sivi/Sivi burgundac is Pinot Gris; Pinot Grigio is an alternate name of Pinot Gris.
independence: UC Davis/VIVC-linked synonym lists, Serbian usage and English, German, Russian and Croatian cultivar articles independently agree on the mappings.
missing_definition: Preserve grammatical variants and label language: Serbian often uses Beli/Sivi burgundac, while international labels use Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris or Pinot Grigio.
missing_descriptors: Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris are separate colour mutations within the Pinot family; Pinot Gris berries can be pink-grey although its wine is usually classified as white.
editor_conclusion: Keep the name mapping and write it explicitly once: «бели бургундац (Pinot Blanc), сиви бургундац (Pinot Gris/Grigio)».

comparison: Current winery and guide records document both cultivars in Vojvodina: Zvonko Bogdan grows and bottles both around Palić, Petra grows Pinot Grigio beside Lake Palić, and current Srem entries include Pinot Blanc and Pinot Grigio wines.
independence: Official producer specifications, an official local wine route and an independent current tasting guide provide separate named examples.
missing_definition: Regional presence is not a vineyard-share statement; Vojvodina covers several wine regions and the book gives no date or planted-hectare total.
missing_descriptors: Current styles range from clear still whites to blends and skin-contact/orange Pinot Grigio, so one shared «Vojvodina style» should not be inferred.
editor_conclusion: Keep «Воеводина» as a broad distribution label, preferably with examples from Subotica/Palić and Srem rather than an implied exclusive centre.

comparison: The pair is visibly part of modern portfolios and Zvonko Bogdan Pinot Blanc 2022 scored 95 in a current guide. Yet the 2024 commercial register's four leading whites are Grašac, Chardonnay, Riesling and Sauvignon Blanc; neither Pinot appears, and no Vojvodina-specific area table makes them a measured foundation.
independence: Official winery plantings prove modern use, while the register-derived national hierarchy and a current multi-producer guide provide independent scale and quality context.
missing_definition: «Foundation» must specify whether it means hectares, number of labels, new-planting approvals, prestige bottlings or one subregion's producer mix, and must carry a date.
missing_descriptors: Pinot Blanc has a four-hectare named Palić block at one major producer, but that single estate figure cannot be generalized to Serbia or all Vojvodina.
editor_conclusion: Replace the unmeasured superlative with «заметная часть современного ассортимента Воеводины» unless a dated regional planting table is added.

comparison: Palić has strong named evidence for both varieties, including a four-hectare Pinot Blanc block and Petra Pinot Grigio. The soil clause is too broad: the Subotica–Horgoš sandland contains multiple soil types, and Petra's lakeside vineyard is explicitly clay- and loam-rich rather than pure sand.
independence: Two official producer/tourism records establish the wines and sites; a peer-reviewed regional study independently documents soil heterogeneity.
missing_definition: Distinguish the Palić wine location, the wider geomorphological peščara and the measured soil of a particular parcel; they are not interchangeable denominators.
missing_descriptors: Arenosol and shifting sand coexist with clay, chernozem-with-sand and brown steppe soils, while groundwater and irrigation further alter vine response.
editor_conclusion: Keep Palić as a modern centre for examples, but replace «на песках Палича» with named parcel evidence or «в неоднородном песчано-лёссовом ландшафте вокруг Палича».

comparison: A current Župa inventory names Sémillon, and two Negotin producers document it at Rajac and Smedovac in varietal and blended wines. These are direct named-presence records, although none quantifies regional hectares.
independence: A regional producer history, two separate official winery records and a tourism inventory converge across both named regions.
missing_definition: The labels identify wine regions, not exclusivity or scale; the variety also has a documented modern example in Šumadija.
missing_descriptors: Negotin evidence includes both a varietal dry label and a Sauvignon blend; Župa evidence presently establishes planting, not a current named varietal release.
editor_conclusion: Keep «Жупа, Неготин» as examples of current presence, without implying that they are the only Serbian locations.

comparison: Current producer language independently calls Sémillon rare and available at only a few Serbian wineries. Historical sources place it in the royal Oplenac assortment by the late 1920s, while present records show new and active examples; no source traces an unbroken Župa or Negotin parcel from that era to today.
independence: Official current producers establish rarity and present use; two Serbian historical accounts independently preserve the Oplenac list, though both may draw on the same local institutional memory.
missing_definition: «Yugoslav times» must distinguish the interwar kingdom from socialist Yugoslavia and must not be mistaken for vine age or genetic continuity of a parcel.
missing_descriptors: Eden's Sémillon vineyard was planted only in 2014–2015, demonstrating that present Serbian Sémillon includes recent plantings as well as historical memory.
editor_conclusion: Write «редкий сорт, документированный в Сербии как минимум с конца 1920-х и вновь представленный несколькими современными хозяйствами»; omit the unproved continuity claim.

comparison: The French national variety catalogue describes full-bodied dry wines with moderate-to-low acidity, while English and German cultivar articles describe heavy/oily or powerful Sémillon. Serbian producer records, however, show dry, blended and naturally sweet expressions and do not all publish acidity or wax descriptors.
independence: An INRAE/IFV technical catalogue and multilingual reference works agree on the cultivar's potential; three independent Serbian winery records demonstrate stylistic variation.
missing_definition: Separate intrinsic potential from a measured wine: «low acidity» needs titratable acidity, pH, harvest date and vintage, while «waxy» needs a named tasting source.
missing_descriptors: Current local profiles include citrus freshness and mineral finish in the Aglaja blend, dry varietal Zenit and ripe fig, concentration, full body and sweetness in Eden 2018.
editor_conclusion: Retain as a qualified varietal tendency—«может давать полнотелые, умеренно кислотные, восково-маслянистые вина»—then describe named Serbian bottles separately.

comparison: One current Negotin blend is documented, but so are two 100% Sémillon labels from Negotin and Šumadija. A handful of products cannot establish a national frequency, and no register or current complete portfolio census classifies Sémillon output by blend versus varietal wine.
independence: The three winery records are primary and mutually independent, but the sample is small, uneven by vintage and not designed as a census.
missing_definition: «More often» needs a date and denominator—active labels, litres, vineyard hectares, producers or releases—and must decide whether archived and sold-out wines count.
missing_descriptors: The blend-versus-varietal distinction says nothing by itself about dry, sweet, skin-contact, oak or ageing style.
editor_conclusion: Delete the frequency claim or replace it with the verifiable formulation «в Сербии встречается и в купажах, и в редких сортовых бутылках».

comparison: The national centre's commercial-vineyard inventory says Cabernet is grown across Serbia and places its largest areas in Tri Morave, Srem and Šumadija, not Negotinska Krajina. Negotin nevertheless has strong regional identity, regulatory presence and internationally recognised examples.
independence: The planting hierarchy comes from the specialist national centre; ministry regional material, expert interviews and current wines independently establish Negotin's qualitative importance without changing the area ranking.
missing_definition: «First and foremost» must specify planted hectares, output, label count, score, reputation or a traveller's recommendation; these produce different regional hierarchies.
missing_descriptors: Negotin reds are officially characterised as extracted and higher-alcohol while retaining acids, aroma and colour through fresh nights, but this applies to the protected regional style, not every Cabernet.
editor_conclusion: Replace with «один из главных терруарных ориентиров — Неготинская Крайина»; do not present Negotin as the largest Cabernet region.

comparison: French technical data and English, German and Russian reference articles agree on deep colour, firm tannic structure and blackcurrant at proper maturity; cedar and tobacco are repeatedly associated with oak and age. Kremen Kamen 2021 confirms blackcurrant and cedar, while a 2020 Kremen note includes tobacco.
independence: INRAE/IFV varietal data, multilingual reference works, a competition tasting and an independent Serbian product tasting converge on the profile's core.
missing_definition: Name the wine and vintage; distinguish primary fruit and tannin from oak- and bottle-derived cedar, tobacco, coffee, leather and related tertiary notes.
missing_descriptors: Kremen Kamen 2021 additionally shows blackberry, plum, coffee-oak, earth and herbs; current Serbian Cabernets also show redcurrant, pepper, mint and leather.
editor_conclusion: Keep the descriptors as a possible Cabernet/Kremen profile, prefaced by «часто» and tied to one or more dated vintages.

comparison: Matalj Kremen Kamen 2021 was judged complex, precise and balanced, and the ministry's regional profile explains how fresh nights can preserve aromatic complexity and acids despite high alcohol. Yet the same current national tasting corpus explicitly finds jammy, very ripe, sweet-fruited and 15–15.5% Cabernet examples, so the national generalisation fails.
independence: A ministry regional account and independent tastings support balanced eastern examples; the multi-producer guide independently supplies counterexamples from the wider Serbian scene.
missing_definition: «Overripe» needs a sensory or analytical threshold and must be separated from high alcohol, oak sweetness and fully ripe tannins; producer, wine, vintage and taster are essential.
missing_descriptors: Green/herbal, red-fruited, jammy, precise, warm, oxidative and oak-sweet styles all occur in the current sample, preventing one Serbian Cabernet profile.
editor_conclusion: Write «лучшие восточные примеры, включая Kremen, сочетают зрелый плод со свежестью» and delete the claim about Serbian Cabernet as a whole.

comparison: Danas quotes Petrović directly calling Negotinska Krajina ideal for four black cultivars including Cabernet Sauvignon. NIN later quotes him describing the area's Cabernet as good, full and rounded and the terroir as recognisable.
independence: These are two direct interviews with the same expert, so they secure attribution but are not independent scientific confirmation; separate ministry material provides compatible regional context.
missing_definition: «Ideal» is Petrović's qualitative expert assessment and applies to a heterogeneous region with five vinogorja, not a measured universal optimum for every parcel.
missing_descriptors: The later interview adds Gamay and Začinak to the recognisable full, rounded red-wine zone and cautions against reducing the region to Cabernet alone.
editor_conclusion: Keep the sentence explicitly as Petrović's view and include the wider list or narrow it to «он относит край к идеальным зонам для каберне».

comparison: The official DWWA result and Decanter's complete 2026 Platinum list identify Matalj Kremen Kamen 2021, Negotinska Krajina, at 97 points and Platinum. The judges' note supports exceptional complexity and balance, but one winning wine cannot validate a region-wide causal claim.
independence: The searchable results database and Decanter editorial list are two publications of the same competition; an independent current guide also scored the wine 96, corroborating quality but not the exact DWWA award.
missing_definition: State DWWA, wine, vintage and score. «Confirmation» should mean evidence of high potential, not proof that Petrović's comparative word «ideal» is scientifically established.
missing_descriptors: DWWA records blackberry, blackcurrant, plum, cedar, coffee-oak, earth and herbs; these belong to the 2021 wine, not every Kremen vintage.
editor_conclusion: Keep «Kremen Kamen 2021 — 97 баллов и платина DWWA 2026»; rephrase the link as an illustration of potential rather than proof of regional ideality.

comparison: CEVVIN ranks Merlot second among all commercial vineyard cultivars, immediately behind Grašac, and Cabernet Sauvignon third. A current guide citing the 2024 register independently reports 11% Merlot, 9% Cabernet Sauvignon and 5% Prokupac, making Merlot the leading red and international red by planted share.
independence: CEVVIN and the guide are separate specialist publications but may ultimately draw on the same national vineyard-register system; their ranking and percentages are mutually compatible rather than fully independent censuses.
missing_definition: «Most widespread» must mean current commercial planted area, not number of wineries, labels, bottles, regions or all household vines; «everywhere» must not imply equal density.
missing_descriptors: The strongest current concentrations are Tri Morave, Srem and Leskovac, and CEVVIN places much of the area at 300–400 m on southern or south-eastern exposures.
editor_conclusion: Keep «самый распространённый международный красный по площади коммерческих посадок» and replace «повсюду» with «широко выращивается по стране; крупнейшие площади — в Трёх Моравах, Среме и Лесковце».

comparison: The French technical catalogue characterises Merlot as round, full-bodied and structured with relatively low acidity and rather supple tannins; multilingual references repeatedly add plum, cherry and red-berry fruit. Current Serbian tastings reproduce those notes but also show firm tannin, high alcohol, jamminess and considerable oak-driven variation.
independence: INRAE/IFV varietal evidence and the independent 268-wine Serbian guide are methodologically different and converge on potential softness and plum fruit while the guide supplies direct local counterexamples to a uniform profile.
missing_definition: «Usually» needs a dated denominator and sampling method; «soft» and «moderate tannin» need either a named tasting or analytical/phenolic criteria and must be separated from ripe tannin and oak texture.
missing_descriptors: Serbian examples also show raspberry, blackberry, redcurrant, mint, eucalyptus, tobacco, graphite, vegetal notes, sweet oak, jam and alcohol warmth, with tannins ranging from supple to firm.
editor_conclusion: Retain as a qualified tendency: «часто встречаются слива и красная вишня; танины могут быть мягкими, но стиль зависит от места, зрелости и выдержки».

comparison: The current guide supplies examples on both sides of the proposed divide but no matched north–south experiment or representative regional averages. Northern Srem alone includes lively, elegant Merlot and jammy, warm 15% examples; central and eastern wines likewise span fresh, ripe, firm and dense styles.
independence: The guide is broad and independent but is one critic's non-random producer sample; general cultivar sources explain climate sensitivity without testing Serbian regional means.
missing_definition: Define north and south, select comparable vintages and winemaking, and measure freshness and density through acidity, pH, alcohol, extract, phenolics or blinded sensory scores.
missing_descriptors: Altitude, exposure, soil, diurnal range, yield, harvest date, alcohol, oak regime and bottle age can all confound latitude; CEVVIN's largest Merlot areas themselves span Tri Morave, Srem and Leskovac.
editor_conclusion: Delete the national binary. If retained, use named examples—such as an elegant Subotica wine and a dense Negotin wine—without presenting them as a proven latitude rule.

comparison: The official DWWA 2025 record and Decanter's editorial selection identify Zvonko Bogdan Merlot 2023 from Palić/Subotica at 95 points and Gold. The New Europe Wine Guide later gives it 94, demonstrating normal critic variation and not changing the exact competition result.
independence: The DWWA database and Decanter article are two publications of the same award, so they secure attribution but are not independent judgments; the 2026 guide is independent and uses its own score.
missing_definition: Write the full event and year—Decanter World Wine Awards 2025—and distinguish a DWWA medal score from a general Decanter review.
missing_descriptors: DWWA describes ripe blackberry, cassis, tobacco, cedar, concentrated palate, inky tannin and mouth-watering acidity; the independent guide instead emphasises red cherry, raspberry, mint, precision and ripe tannin.
editor_conclusion: Keep as «Zvonko Bogdan Merlot 2023 — золото и 95 баллов DWWA 2025»; do not merge the 95 with the guide's separate 94-point tasting.

comparison: Current primary producer pages confirm Pinot Noir in both named locations: a varietal still red from Oplenac and a varietal rosé plus a rosé blend from Knjaževac. The compressed place list hides this material difference in wine type and says nothing about vineyard area or regional importance.
independence: Aleksandrović and Džervin are independent primary records from different regions; official zoning and a regional overview provide separate geographical context, while the multilingual Wikipedia corpus only establishes national/general background.
missing_definition: Specify whether the heading means vineyards, current commercial wines or recommended places to taste Pinot Noir, and identify the colour/style in each place.
missing_descriptors: The Oplenac evidence is a still red from Bokanja; the direct current Knjaževac evidence is rosé, including one 100% Pinot Noir and one 50% blend with Muscat Hamburg.
editor_conclusion: Retain both place names but write them asymmetrically: «красный пино нуар с Опленца; в Княжевце есть как минимум актуальные розовые версии».

comparison: Current producer evidence and an independent guide establish credible named Šumadija Pinot Noirs. The guide's two identified regional examples score 89 and Pinot Noir is reviewed in several other Serbian regions, so neither exceptional regional performance nor the adverb 'unexpectedly' follows from the corpus.
independence: The independent 268-wine guide is separate from producer promotion and confirms that the regional wines are real reviewable examples, but its sample is not a controlled regional ranking; the six Wikipedias supply no local comparison.
missing_definition: Define 'well' by scores, consistency, awards, vineyard area or market success; define the expected baseline and compare a representative Šumadija sample with other Serbian regions in matched vintages.
missing_descriptors: Named examples show red cherry, strawberry, raspberry, grippy or grainy tannin, oak, coffee, vanilla and occasional vegetal notes rather than one uniform regional profile.
editor_conclusion: Replace the evaluative generalisation with evidence: «в Шумадии есть заметные коммерческие пино нуары, включая вина с Опленца»; reserve quality judgments for named wines and attributed scores.

comparison: Official zoning and specialist regional evidence support Knjaževac as a mountain-influenced, elevated and comparatively cooler Serbian vineyard setting; independent cultivar references consistently place Pinot Noir in cool to moderate climates and warn against excessive heat. This supports the direction of the sentence, not an absolute climate label.
independence: Government zoning supplies local environmental evidence, while multilingual cultivar references independently supply Pinot Noir's general climate response. They are complementary rather than repetitions of one source.
missing_definition: Attach a reference period and station or use bioclimatic indices, growing-degree days and diurnal range; state the comparison set behind 'cool'.
missing_descriptors: Elevation, exposure, valley inversions, annual and growing-season temperature, rainfall, frost and vintage variation matter more than a single adjective.
editor_conclusion: Use relative wording: «в сравнительно прохладных и высотных участках Княжевца»; do not turn the shorthand into a formal climate classification.

comparison: Duck and mushroom risotto are direct producer recommendations for the Oplenac Trijumf Noir, making the pairing defensible for that named wine. Džervin's current Knjaževac Pinot Noir rosé is instead paired with fish and grilled dishes; its Pinot-based blend includes chicken recommendations but not mushrooms.
independence: The pairing evidence consists of two independent producers' serving recommendations, which are primary for intended use but subjective and commercial. General cultivar sources do not establish food pairing, and no independent Knjaževac sensory panel links local Pinot Noir specifically to mushrooms.
missing_definition: Identify the wine colour, structure and preparation method: roast duck, chicken salad and mushroom risotto impose different weight, fat and sauce requirements.
missing_descriptors: Acidity, tannin, oak, alcohol, fruit concentration, sauce and cooking method should drive the pairing; current Knjaževac evidence is rosé rather than the red profile assumed by a classic mushroom pairing.
editor_conclusion: Keep as named advice, not regional law: «Trijumf Noir с Опленца производитель рекомендует к утке и грибному ризотто; для княжевацких розе нужны иные пары».

comparison: Current primary and specialist records place Frankovka/Kékfrankos in both zones: Verkat and Maurer document Fruška Gora fruit, while Maurer's Subotica holdings list Kékfrankos. The heading is geographically sound but compresses very different scales and production contexts.
independence: The Serbian regulatory table independently anchors Fruška Gora, while Maurer's current technical profile supplies direct evidence from one producer working both Fruška Gora and Subotica; multilingual references place Serbian Frankovka more generally in Vojvodina.
missing_definition: State whether the place names mean permitted cultivar, planted vineyard, current wine or regional concentration; acreage and producer counts would be needed for importance.
missing_descriptors: The direct examples include a Fruška Gora varietal Kékfrankos, a Fruška Gora Frankovka-led Cabernet Franc blend and Subotica Kékfrankos used both in plantings and blends.
editor_conclusion: Keep both zones as occurrence points: «встречается на Фрушке горе и в Суботице»; do not imply equal acreage or dominance.

comparison: VIVC 1459 and the multilingual corpus agree that Frankovka, Blaufränkisch, Kékfrankos and Limberger forms denote the same cultivar. The Serbian book label and German cross-reference are therefore correct.
independence: VIVC is the authoritative cultivar registry; German, English, Hungarian, Russian and Croatian encyclopedic traditions independently reproduce the same central synonym mapping.
missing_definition: Use one prime name plus local synonym and preserve diacritics: «Frankovka (Blaufränkisch; венг. Kékfrankos)». Avoid treating every historical homonym such as Gamé as Gamay Noir.
missing_descriptors: Identity should be kept separate from origin, pedigree and wine style; synonyms do not imply identical regional vinification.
editor_conclusion: Retain the identification and standardise the spelling across the book.

comparison: Pronounced or lively acidity recurs across VIVC-linked technical traditions, multilingual references and current Serbian wines. Body and density are variable: German evidence explicitly spans light fruity to powerful tannic wines, while Serbian examples range from light refreshing blends to structured oak-aged bottlings.
independence: General cultivar references and two current Serbian producer lines converge on acidity but not on a single density. The producer and importer records are independent commercial sources, though neither is a representative national survey.
missing_definition: Replace «density» with body, tannin, extract or concentration and specify whether the profile describes the cultivar's potential or sampled Serbian bottles.
missing_descriptors: Common additions are dark or red cherry, berries, spice, pepper and tannin; harvest date, yield, maceration, blending and oak can materially change weight and structure.
editor_conclusion: Qualify the profile: «обычно сохраняет живую кислотность; тело меняется от лёгкого до плотного в зависимости от урожая и винификации».

comparison: The vino.rs 2025 annual selection explicitly lists FRANKOVKA 2023 VERKAT as Best Buy among red wines from international cultivars. Current Verkat and retail records identify the label as FranFrankovka and document the established 85% Frankovka/15% Cabernet Franc composition.
independence: Vino.rs is the sole authority for its own editorial award. Producer and retailer evidence independently clarify wine identity and composition but do not create a second award judgment.
missing_definition: Name the awarding publication and category; Best Buy here is a vino.rs editorial price-to-quality designation, not an official competition medal.
missing_descriptors: The wine is a Frankovka-led blend with Cabernet Franc, red berries, spice, green pepper, oak-derived vanilla, freshness and additional structure from the second cultivar.
editor_conclusion: Write: «FranFrankovka 2023 Verkat, купаж Frankovka и Cabernet Franc, вошла у vino.rs в Best Buy 2025 среди красных международных сортов».

comparison: Current official and regional evidence firmly places Gamay in Negotinska Krajina. CEVVIN names it among the cultivar's three largest Serbian commercial zones; NIN lists it among the region's most represented international cultivars; the local tourism authority and active producers document multiple varietal and blended wines.
independence: CEVVIN supplies national commercial-area context, a current regional feature records vineyards and expert evidence, and independent monastery and private-winery portfolios demonstrate market presence. Serbian Wikipedia adds an older quantified example from Ključko vinogorje.
missing_definition: Use «Неготинская Крайина» rather than the city alone and distinguish regional occurrence from dominance; exact hectares, vintages and a dated producer count would be needed for a market-share claim.
missing_descriptors: Current forms include still red, barrique, reserve, rosé and blends with Začinak or other cultivars, so the place label covers more than one wine style.
editor_conclusion: Retain the geography as «Гаме · Неготинская Крайина» without implying that every vineyard or wine in the region uses the cultivar.

comparison: None of the current official, regional, producer or six-language Wikipedia sources dates the first, renewed or continuous Negotinska Krajina Gamay plantings to the 1960s. Raj's Game 2017 is said to come from vines over forty years old, but the reference point and planting year are not precise enough to establish that decade.
independence: Several independent source types prove current and multi-decade presence, but all fail at the same historical question. A promotional tourism reference to pre-phylloxera Gamay is ambiguous about whether it describes cultivar, vine material or vineyard age and cannot repair the gap.
missing_definition: Specify whether 1960s means first introduction, industrial expansion, replanting after an interruption or the age of a surviving parcel; then supply a dated planting register, nursery record, school archive or winery ledger.
missing_descriptors: A vineyard name, planting year, clone or massal source, rootstock, owner and evidence of continuity would turn the broad date into an auditable historical statement.
editor_conclusion: Remove «с 1960-х». If no archive is found, use only the supported wording: «в регионе сорт укоренён уже несколько десятилетий».

comparison: English, German, Hungarian and Russian references plus Vin de France support light body and raspberry, strawberry, cherry or other berry fruit as common Gamay profiles. The local evidence cuts against treating them as the Negotin norm: Raj explicitly contrasts its fuller, more intense and ageworthy wines with light French Gamay, while Petrović calls regional Gamay full and rounded.
independence: The general style recurs across several language traditions and an official French varietal portal. Two independent Negotinska Krajina sources, one producer and one named expert in national press, independently document fuller local examples, though neither is a representative blind regional survey.
missing_definition: State whether the adjectives describe the cultivar's international tendency, a young carbonic-maceration style or sampled Negotin bottles; define body through alcohol, extract, tannin, maceration and ageing rather than a single adjective.
missing_descriptors: Common general notes include raspberry, strawberry, cherry, blackberry, florals and refreshing acidity; local fuller versions add intensity, structure, freshness and longer ageing potential.
editor_conclusion: Qualify the contrast: «гаме часто бывает лёгким и ягодным, но неготинские версии могут быть полнее и рассчитаны на выдержку».

comparison: Gamay is plainly established rather than a one-off novelty in Negotinska Krajina: CEVVIN reports significant commercial area, current reporting records monastery plantings, the municipal directory lists many local labels and styles, and Raj describes a wine from vines over forty years old.
independence: An official specialist body, a municipal tourism authority, national press and several producers converge on sustained regional presence. They are independent for occurrence and portfolio breadth, though promotional sources cannot establish an exact beginning date.
missing_definition: Replace the metaphor «не экзотика» with a testable meaning such as multiple active producers, commercial vineyard area or decades-old vines; do not convert that evidence into the unsupported 1960s date.
missing_descriptors: The cultivar appears across monastery, family and commercial portfolios and in red, reserve, barrel-aged, rosé and blended wines, which demonstrates breadth better than the informal label.
editor_conclusion: Retain the idea as «давно укоренился в Неготинской Крайине» and keep it logically separate from any exact planting decade.

comparison: VIVC identifies Teroldego as an Italian black wine grape, while Italian registration records, the English and German encyclopedic corpus and specialist regional evidence consistently centre it on Trentino and Campo Rotaliano. The book's northern-Italian identification is sound.
independence: VIVC independently fixes cultivar identity and country; the Italian national registry anchors recognised material in Trentino; English and German references separately reproduce the historical and commercial regional concentration.
missing_definition: Distinguish country of origin from the cultivar's historical centre: VIVC says Italy, while the more precise Trentino or Piana Rotaliana association comes from distribution, documentation and clonal context.
missing_descriptors: The exact birthplace and the competing etymologies are not needed here; VIVC number 12371 and the Trentino concentration are the stable identifying details.
editor_conclusion: Retain as «североитальянский сорт, исторически сосредоточенный в Трентино».

comparison: English and German distribution summaries show a heavy Italian and Trentino concentration and only small holdings elsewhere; current Serbian reporting likewise calls Šapat's wine a local rarity. Teroldego is nevertheless planted in several countries, so «rare» must mean low and scattered presence rather than absence outside Trentino.
independence: The multilingual distribution record, an official Serbian cultivar register and independent Serbian wine reporting cover different levels: global concentration, legal recognition and one current commercial example. None supplies a complete 2026 worldwide hectare table, but all point in the same direction.
missing_definition: Name the denominator and date behind rarity: global planted area, country count, Serbian hectares, producer count or label count. Avoid equating concentration in Trentino with exclusivity to Trentino.
missing_descriptors: Known external pockets include the United States, Brazil, Australia, New Zealand and Serbia; these exceptions should be acknowledged if the sentence is expanded.
editor_conclusion: Keep with a qualifier: «за пределами Трентино встречается редко, хотя небольшие посадки есть в нескольких странах».

comparison: Šapat's current primary page lists Teroldego among its own vineyard cultivars and Terol 2022 as a 100% varietal wine; independent 2025 reporting confirms the Serbian bottling. The heading compresses two nearby place labels: the complex has a Novi Slankamen address, while the producer locates the vines in Slankamenački Vinogradi.
independence: The producer is authoritative for its vineyard and wine, the Serbian ministry register independently confirms Teroldego is recognised in the country, and Vino.rs independently reports the varietal wine and estate fruit.
missing_definition: Say whether Novi Slankamen denotes postal address, winery complex or vineyard. For exact vineyard geography use Slankamenački Vinogradi; for a short visitor-facing heading Novi Slankamen is acceptable.
missing_descriptors: Current primary details are Terol 2022, 100% Teroldego, 13.5% alcohol and used-barrique ageing; production volume is inconsistent between sources and should be omitted until reconciled.
editor_conclusion: Write: «Šapat у Новом Сланкамене выращивает терольдего на участке в Сланкаменачки-Виногради и выпускает сортовой Terol».

comparison: The producer directly documents Teroldego, Blaufränkisch and Merlot within the same vineyard estate, mainly southern hill slopes at 210–235 metres, deep calcareous loess below a thin chernozem layer and views toward the Danube. Independent reporting confirms the southern slope and estate planting period. What is not documented is row-by-row adjacency.
independence: Šapat supplies the detailed cultivar, altitude and soil profile; Vino.rs independently places the relevant 2011–2012 vineyards on the sunny slope above Slankamen. The two sources converge on setting but do not provide a parcel map.
missing_definition: Replace «рядом» with «в том же хозяйстве» unless a block map proves adjacency. Describe the soil as chernozem over loess, not bare loess, and treat the Danube wording as landscape orientation rather than a measured river-distance claim.
missing_descriptors: Useful site details are southern exposure, 210–235 metres, ventilation, lean well-drained soil and a lime-bearing loess sublayer; parcel, clone, row orientation and cultivar-specific hectares remain absent.
editor_conclusion: Use: «в том же хозяйстве растут франковка и мерло; участки лежат на южном склоне, где тонкий чернозём перекрывает глубокий лёсс, с видом на Дунай».

comparison: The heading works as a union of examples: official and current sources document Cabernet Franc and Marselan in Toplica, Cabernet Franc, Marselan and Syrah in Šumadija, and current Cabernet Franc and Marselan wines in Negotinska Krajina. They do not support the stronger reading that all three cultivars occur in all three places; Petrović specifically describes Syrah as missing from Negotinska Krajina, and no clean current Toplica Syrah record was found.
independence: Government zoning and regulation establish region boundaries and cultivar context; an independent 268-wine guide, a current market list and two official competition records supply named wines; a professor's interview independently warns against the Negotin–Syrah inference. These sources differ in purpose and converge only at the collective-list level.
missing_definition: Turn the compressed heading into explicit mappings or say «встречаются, среди прочего, в Топлице, Шумадии и Неготинской Крайине». Never transfer a Potrkanje/Knjaževac wine to Negotin merely because both lie in eastern Serbia.
missing_descriptors: For a rigorous map give producer, wine, vineyard or village, vintage and evidence date for each cultivar–region pair; current evidence remains incomplete for Syrah in Toplica and Negotinska Krajina.
editor_conclusion: Retain the three regions only as a collective list and add explicit examples; do not imply a complete three-by-three planting matrix.

comparison: Current wines and the 2019 register show that all three cultivars exist in Serbia and that Marselan then occupied a small area, but no source defines or dates one shared «young wave». The multilingual Wikipedia corpus contains cultivar histories, not Serbian planting cohorts, while current labels cannot distinguish young vines from newly released brands.
independence: Official statistics, regional zoning, a broad tasting guide and market evidence are independent for presence, yet none supplies planting years or a before-and-after series for all three cultivars. Their common silence is a data gap rather than negative proof.
missing_definition: Define «young» and «wave»: for example plantings after 2000, share of vines under fifteen years, hectares added between two register snapshots or a documented boutique-winery movement. Separate vineyard planting from first commercial release.
missing_descriptors: Needed evidence includes parcel planting year, area by cultivar at two or more dates, nursery or register records and named producers; Marselan's 1961 creation date is not a Serbian planting date.
editor_conclusion: Remove the unmeasured slogan or rewrite it as an attributed observation about post-2000 boutique portfolios with dated examples.

comparison: English, German and Serbian references support Cabernet Franc as generally lighter, less tannic or less powerful than Cabernet Sauvignon. Serbian tastings include Lastar's elegant, lightly grippy Cabernet Franc, but the same current guide also records a rich, opulent 16% example. The general varietal tendency is sound; the Serbia-wide «usually» is not demonstrated.
independence: The structural comparison recurs across three language traditions, though their shared wine literature is not fully independent. The current Serbian guide supplies multiple named countervailing examples but is not a random matched Cabernet Franc–Cabernet Sauvignon survey.
missing_definition: Specify whether «lighter» means alcohol, colour, extract, body or tannin and whether the comparison controls producer, site, vintage and élevage. National frequency requires a representative sample.
missing_descriptors: Serbian examples range from light and elegant to bold, sweet-fruited and opulent; tannins range from soft or slight grip to more substantial structures depending on ripeness and winemaking.
editor_conclusion: Write the comparison as a cultivar tendency, not a measured Serbian rule: «обычно легче и менее танинный, чем каберне совиньон, хотя сербские версии бывают и очень спелыми, плотными».

comparison: Raspberry and bell or green pepper recur in the English and Serbian Cabernet Franc corpus, and the current Serbian guide directly gives graphite and red berry fruit for Lastar Cabernet Franc 2020. Named Serbian blends also show raspberry and red pepper. The terms are plausible but not universal, and green character changes with ripeness.
independence: Multilingual encyclopedic summaries establish general varietal vocabulary, while an independent current tasting guide supplies Serbian wine-level examples. The latter covers several wines but not a controlled national aroma-frequency study.
missing_definition: Present the words as possible or common notes rather than a mandatory three-note signature. Clarify whether «зелёный перец» means bell pepper and distinguish varietal pyrazine character from under-ripe fruit.
missing_descriptors: Other documented Cabernet Franc notes include violet, tobacco leaf, red berries, cassis, carob, dark chocolate and spice; oak and blending can materially change the profile.
editor_conclusion: Keep with modal wording: «может давать малину, сладкий или зелёный перец и графит; выраженность зелёных нот зависит от зрелости».

comparison: Plantgrape directly records that INRA obtained Marselan in 1961 from Cabernet Sauvignon and Grenache. English, German and Russian Wikipedia independently reproduce the same date and parents, and the Rhône varietal portal agrees.
independence: The French national technical catalogue is the primary authority; the Rhône body is a separate institutional summary, while the three Wikipedias are useful corroboration but partly derivative. No material contradiction was found.
missing_definition: If expanded, name INRA and distinguish the 1961 crossing from later registration, commercial adoption and Serbian planting dates.
missing_descriptors: The stable identity details are France, INRA, 1961 and Cabernet Sauvignon × Grenache; naming order does not alter the parentage claim.
editor_conclusion: Retain: «марселан — французское скрещивание каберне совиньона и гренаша, полученное INRA в 1961 году».

comparison: Small berries, thick skins and some disease tolerance are real Marselan traits, but the book incorrectly converts traits into the original breeding purpose. The detailed historical accounts say the programme sought productive large-berried material and initially shelved Marselan because the berries were too small; disease tolerance drove later reconsideration. Plantgrape also shows selective susceptibility, so «устойчивость к болезням» is too broad.
independence: English and Russian historical summaries agree on the programme reversal; Plantgrape independently documents very small berries and a mixed disease profile; the Rhône portal independently confirms thick skin and rot resistance. Together they separate history from present traits.
missing_definition: Distinguish breeding objective, reason for initial rejection and later valued traits. Name the diseases: low grey-rot susceptibility and limited powdery-mildew sensitivity do not equal general resistance, because young leaves remain susceptible to downy mildew and phylloxeric galls.
missing_descriptors: Very small berries limit juice yield; the Rhône portal describes thick skins, intense bluish colour at ripeness, rot resistance and drought sensitivity. None makes small berries the original desired outcome.
editor_conclusion: Replace with: «сорт сначала отложили из-за слишком мелкой ягоды; позже к нему вернулись благодаря качеству вина и устойчивости прежде всего к серой гнили».

comparison: Plantgrape and the Rhône portal agree on strong colour, aromatic intensity and supple, harmonious or non-bitter tannins; the latter explicitly gives ripe red and black fruit. The berries themselves are dark and bluish at ripeness. The substance is correct, but «чёрные ягоды» conflates grape colour with a black-fruit tasting note.
independence: Two French institutional sources independently cover technical wine potential and regional varietal description; English, German and Russian encyclopedic pages broadly corroborate colour and tannin. Their agreement is strong for traits, not for every Serbian bottling.
missing_definition: Say either «ароматы чёрных ягод» for the wine or «мелкая тёмно-синяя ягода» for morphology. Replace «густой цвет» with «насыщенный цвет» unless viscosity or extract is actually measured.
missing_descriptors: Authoritative profiles add full body, anthocyanin concentration, ripe red fruit, aromatic intensity, acidity-supported balance and ageing potential; Serbian examples can still vary by blend and élevage.
editor_conclusion: Use: «даёт насыщенно окрашенные, ароматные вина с нотами спелых красных и чёрных фруктов и мягким, не горьким танином».

comparison: The 2019 CEVVIN table unambiguously lists Marselan at 20.21 hectares on 24 parcels. The value 40 appears on the immediately following Župski Bojadiser row, showing a row-alignment transcription error rather than an alternative Marselan estimate.
independence: One authoritative dated table resolves the exact arithmetic; the multilingual Wikipedia corpus contains no Serbian parcel statistic and therefore offers no competing value. Independent current wines prove continued presence but cannot update the register count.
missing_definition: Retain the register date and scope: this is a 1 March 2019 commercial-vineyard snapshot, not a timeless current total. Do not infer present area from the 2019 figure without a later comparable table.
missing_descriptors: The same table records Syrah at 34.32 hectares on 56 parcels; adding row labels to any transcription would prevent another shifted-value error.
editor_conclusion: Correct to «20,21 га на 24 участках по данным реестра на 1 марта 2019 года».

comparison: All six language checks support climate- and ripeness-driven Syrah variation; pepper, violet and smoke are valid descriptors, while ripe and jammy styles are equally recognised. Current Serbian evidence is internally diverse: it includes lean black-pepper, smoky and fresh examples, juicy modern fruit and a 15.5% powerful, ripe, flamboyant Shiraz. No random sample measures which style is more frequent.
independence: The general climate model recurs across several language traditions, though not all are independent. The current Serbian guide covers many producers and Decanter supplies a separate high-ripeness example; both disprove a binary but neither establishes national prevalence.
missing_definition: Define «старосветский ключ» analytically and specify the denominator for «чаще»: labels, hectares, producers, blind-tasted wines or sales. Syrah-versus-Shiraz naming alone is not a reliable style classifier.
missing_descriptors: Observed Serbian notes include black pepper, smoky bacon, raspberry, strawberry, blueberry, milk chocolate, ripe red fruit, mocha and spicy oak, with alcohol and body ranging widely.
editor_conclusion: Replace the national-frequency claim with a spectrum: «сербская сира бывает и перечной, дымной, более стройной, и очень спелой, мощной; стиль зависит от места, зрелости и винификации».

comparison: Current sources confirm Rkatsiteli in both Župa and Knjaževac. Mozaik explicitly places it on small historical mixed parcels in Župa; Vino.rs calls it an old Knjaževac cultivar, and a 2025 Todorović wine documents 0.9 hectares of local plots. No source dates those Knjaževac vines, and CEVVIN identifies Tri Morave, South Banat and Negotinska Krajina, not Knjaževac, as the three largest national zones.
independence: A Župa producer supplies direct local parcel context, an independent wine publication covers Knjaževac, a current commercial specification supplies plot and vintage detail, and the national viticulture centre gives the broader distribution hierarchy. They independently establish presence but not equal old-vine proof in both places.
missing_definition: Separate present regional occurrence from vine age. Give a vineyard name, planting year and surviving area for Knjaževac before calling its plots old; explain that Župa lies within the wider Tri Morave region.
missing_descriptors: The national 2019 snapshot records 156.87 hectares and thirteenth place, while current large-area regions also include South Banat and Negotinska Krajina; the two-place heading is illustrative, not exhaustive.
editor_conclusion: Use: «сохранился на небольших исторических участках Жупы и по-прежнему выращивается в Княжевацком районе»; не называть княжевацкие лозы старыми без года посадки.

comparison: VIVC authoritatively records RKATSITELI, VIVC 10116, as a blanc Vitis vinifera cultivar from Georgia. CEVVIN, Plantgrape and the English, German and Russian corpus agree on Georgian origin and white-wine use.
independence: VIVC fixes the cultivar identity and country; French and Serbian technical catalogues independently cover use and agronomy; multiple language traditions corroborate the same basic classification.
missing_definition: If expanded, distinguish white-wine use from berry-skin colour and mention that the cultivar is also used as a table grape in its area of origin.
missing_descriptors: Stable identifiers are RKATSITELI, VIVC 10116, Georgia, blanc berry skin and Vitis vinifera; Serbian spellings Rkaciteli and Rkatziteli are recognised forms.
editor_conclusion: Retain: «грузинский белый винный сорт ркацители».

comparison: English and German Wikipedia and Serbian wine media repeatedly call Rkatsiteli one of the oldest cultivars, while Wines of Georgia gives a first-century emergence tradition. VIVC confirms Georgia but supplies no age. Claims that five-thousand-year-old seeds were specifically Rkatsiteli are not accompanied here by modern genetic identification, so the broad word «ancient» is safer than a precise world superlative.
independence: The age formula recurs across encyclopedic and promotional sources but often shares the same traditional seed story. VIVC is independent and authoritative for identity yet silent on age, which lowers confidence in the superlative rather than contradicting ancient cultivation.
missing_definition: Define whether «oldest» means oral tradition, archaeological grape remains, continuous named cultivation, documentary attestation or genetic lineage. Ancient Georgian winemaking is not by itself proof that a seed belongs to the modern named cultivar.
missing_descriptors: A source-backed formulation can state Georgian origin and ancient cultivation tradition without assigning 3000 BCE or an ordinal world rank to the modern genotype.
editor_conclusion: Prefer: «древний грузинский сорт, который часто называют одним из старейших культивируемых»; не давать точную дату без генетически атрибутированного источника.

comparison: CEVVIN securely dates the start of Serbian cultivation to the 1970s, but no reviewed source documents a cultivar-specific state order, mandatory quota or a decision to disregard taste. Mozaik describes postwar industrial wineries and compulsory grape delivery in Župa generally, not an Rkatsiteli allocation.
independence: National technical, regional historical, encyclopedic and wine-media sources all omit the proposed causal mechanism. Their silence cannot prove no directive existed, but it leaves the categorical narrative unsupported.
missing_definition: Name the authority, plan, year, target hectares, receiving combine and archival document behind «разнарядка». Explain what «не из-за вкуса» means and whose preference is being contrasted with policy.
missing_descriptors: A procurement circular, five-year plan, nursery distribution ledger, cooperative planting record or contemporaneous agronomy report is needed; later cultivar traits cannot substitute for motive evidence.
editor_conclusion: Remove the sentence unless an archival directive is found. The supported statement is only: «в Сербии сорт начали выращивать в 1970-х».

comparison: The cultivar was exceptionally widespread in the Soviet Union and reportedly supplied 18% of Soviet wine production by 1978; it also spread to several Black Sea and Eastern European countries. Serbia's technical authority dates local cultivation to the 1970s, not the 1960s. The phrase «throughout the socialist bloc» overstates both geographic completeness and a shared timetable.
independence: English, German and Russian encyclopedic histories converge on Soviet scale, while CEVVIN and Serbian specialist media independently fix Serbia's decade. They do not provide country-by-country planting dates for the entire political bloc.
missing_definition: Replace the political shorthand with named countries and dated evidence. Distinguish the USSR, Yugoslavia and other Eastern European states, whose agricultural systems and planting chronologies were not identical.
missing_descriptors: The secure points are Soviet predominance by 1978, broad Black Sea and Eastern European distribution and Serbian introduction in the 1970s; mass area and exact decade remain country-specific.
editor_conclusion: Write: «в СССР ркацители стал массовым сортом, а в Сербии его начали выращивать в 1970-х; он распространился и в ряде других стран Восточной Европы».

comparison: Strong winter-frost tolerance is consistent across CEVVIN, Plantgrape, Russian Wikipedia and Serbian wine media. Yield is not: Plantgrape says relatively productive, Russian material says generally high but site-dependent, while CEVVIN reports moderate yields, low shoot fruitfulness and long-pruning requirements under Serbian conditions. None proves these traits were the policy reasons for planting.
